## Quick answer: Claude vs ChatGPT by use case

Neither assistant wins everything. Claude Code scored higher than Codex on one independent coding-agent index, Claude lists a context window of up to 1M tokens, and Claude models rank higher on the text leaderboard of LMArena (now Arena, arena.ai). ChatGPT is the better pick for image generation and for the cheaper $8 Go plan. Claude Pro and ChatGPT Plus both cost $20 a month.

**Last verified 16 Oct 2026.** Prices, models and limits come from official pages. Benchmarks come from LMArena and Artificial Analysis. For tool-by-tool data, see the [ChatGPT vs Claude tool comparison](https://trutool.co/compare/chatgpt-vs-claude).

- Image generation: ChatGPT. Anthropic's help center says Claude has no native image generation.
- Lowest paid price: ChatGPT Go at $8 a month, which may show ads.
- Coding agent quality: Claude Code, 68 against 63 for Codex on the Artificial Analysis index. Cost per task: Codex, $1.04 against $14.19 at API rates.
- Longest context window: Claude, up to 1M tokens on paid plans.
- Ad-free assistant: Claude. Anthropic said on 4 Feb 2026 that Claude will remain ad-free.
- Gemini: see the Claude vs ChatGPT vs Gemini section below.

## Claude vs ChatGPT at a glance

![At a glance table of Claude vs ChatGPT winners: coding, writing, images, price, free plan and long documents, verified 16 Oct 2026](/media/c03801d1-5bec-41cf-8e53-0e337c9ea6ee.webp "1600x900")

Claude is Anthropic's assistant and ChatGPT is OpenAI's. Claude's current models are Fable 5.1, Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5 and Haiku 5.5, and ChatGPT runs mainly on the GPT-6 family. Both have a free plan and a $20 standard plan. The table shows which assistant wins each category, and every figure was checked on 16 Oct 2026.


Last checked 16 Oct 2026.

| Category | Claude | ChatGPT | Winner |
|---|---|---|---|
| Coding | Claude Code scored 68 on the Artificial Analysis Coding Agent Index | Codex scored 63, at about one fourteenth of the API cost per task | Claude on quality, ChatGPT on cost |
| Writing | Ranks higher on the LMArena text leaderboard; tone is a matter of taste | Best-ranked OpenAI entry is 21st on the same board | Claude, narrowly |
| Long documents | Up to 1M tokens in chat on paid plans | 256K to 400K tokens for reasoning | Claude |
| Image generation | No native image generation | Yes, on every plan including Free | ChatGPT |
| Voice | Voice mode, listed as beta | Voice with video on Go, Plus and Pro | ChatGPT, on features listed |
| Free plan | $0, session-based limits | $0, unlimited everyday text chats subject to abuse safeguards, may show ads | Tie |
| Price (standard paid) | Pro: $20 a month or $17 a month billed annually | Plus: $20 a month; Go: $8 a month, which may show ads | Tie at $20 a month; ChatGPT cheaper to start, Claude Pro cheaper billed annually |
| Privacy | Training toggle exists; default not confirmed | Personal plans may use chats for training unless you opt out | No call |
| Best for | Developers, long documents, writing | Images, voice, lowest entry price | Depends on the job |

## ChatGPT vs Claude models: what do you get in October 2026?

Both companies changed their lineups in the past two months. Claude's current lineup is four models: Fable 5.1, Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5 and Haiku 5.5. ChatGPT runs mainly on the GPT-6 family (GPT-5.6 Sol is still selectable), with GPT-6.1 Sol limited to ChatGPT Work and Codex. GPT-4o and the other models OpenAI listed on 13 Feb 2026 are retired from ChatGPT. Profiles: [Claude on TruTool](https://trutool.co/tools/claude) and [ChatGPT on TruTool](https://trutool.co/tools/chatgpt).

### Claude models

Last checked 16 Oct 2026.

| Model | Released | Context window | API price per million tokens (input / output) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Claude Fable 5.1 | 1 Sep 2026 | 1M tokens | $10 / $50 |
| Claude Opus 5.5 | 22 Sep 2026 | 1M tokens | $4 / $20 |
| Claude Sonnet 5.5 | 28 Sep 2026 | 1M tokens | $2 / $10 |
| Claude Haiku 5.5 | 7 Oct 2026 | 1M tokens | From $0.10 / $0.50 |

Fable 5.1 is the most expensive of these four models and is not bundled into Claude Pro, where it is billed by usage credits.

### ChatGPT models

Last checked 16 Oct 2026.

| Name in ChatGPT | Where you get it | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| GPT-6 (powered by GPT-6 Sol) | Rolling out to eligible Pro, Plus, Business and Enterprise accounts | The main chat model on paid plans |
| GPT-6 Pro (powered by GPT-6 Astra) | Pro ($100 and $200 per the models help page), Business and Enterprise | The Pro-tier model |
| GPT-6 Luna | Free and Go, per the 7 Oct release note | Help pages still say GPT-5.6 Luna |
| GPT-6.1 Sol | ChatGPT Work and Codex only | Not in the normal chat model picker |

Plus gets the Medium and High settings. Extra High is on Pro, Business and Enterprise. GPT-5.6 Sol can still be selected in the ChatGPT model menu on eligible paid plans. GPT-5.6 Terra and Luna are not selectable in standard chats; they are available in ChatGPT Work and Codex, depending on plan. The models help article and the Free plan help page still say GPT-5.6 Luna, so the exact version is unsettled.

OpenAI's GPT-6 API prices were not verified on an official page, so the API prices above are for Claude only and we do not compare them.

## Which is better overall, Claude or ChatGPT?

Claude has the stronger independent results on the coding-agent index and the text leaderboard, plus a context window of up to 1M tokens. ChatGPT generates images, offers a cheaper $8 plan and has voice with video. On quality alone, the independent data favors Claude. The right pick still depends on the job.

On the LMArena text leaderboard dated 15 Oct 2026, Claude Opus 5.5 ranked 3rd (1508) and the best-ranked OpenAI entry, the older but still selectable GPT-5.6 Sol, ranked 21st (1485). GPT-6 Sol, the model behind ChatGPT's default chat, ranked 61st (1459). On the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index checked on 16 Oct 2026, Opus 5.5 (max effort) scored 58, Sonnet 5.5 (max) 56, and GPT-6 Astra (max) and Fable 5.1 (max) each 53.

LMArena ranks individual models, and matching a model to an app plan is our inference. Scores carry margins of error, so gaps of about 10 points or less are close to ties.

**Where Claude loses:** it cannot generate images, it has no plan between Free and $17 to $20 a month, and Fable 5.1 is not included in Pro. **Where ChatGPT loses:** its best-ranked entry sits 21st on the text leaderboard, Free and Go can show ads in the US, and personal accounts may share data for training unless you opt out.

**Winner: it depends on the job.** Claude for coding quality, long documents and text. ChatGPT for images, voice features and the lowest entry price.

## Claude vs ChatGPT for coding: which is better?

For coding agents, Claude Code scored higher on quality, and Codex cost about 14 times less per task. Artificial Analysis rated Claude Code 68 and Codex 63 on its Coding Agent Index, with Claude Code at $14.19 per task against $1.04 for Codex at API rates. On the LMArena chat coding board, the two are close to a tie.

This is the most direct independent comparison we found of the two coding tools. Artificial Analysis compared both tools on its Coding Agent Index v1.5, checked on 16 Oct 2026. Claude Code ran on Sonnet 5.5 at max effort and Codex ran on GPT-6.1 Sol at extra-high effort.

| Metric (Artificial Analysis, 16 Oct 2026) | Claude Code (Sonnet 5.5) | Codex (GPT-6.1 Sol) |
|---|---|---|
| Coding Agent Index | 68 | 63 |
| DeepSWE v1.1 | 72% | 73% |
| Terminal-Bench 4.0 | 66% | 55% |
| SWE-Atlas-QnA | 67% | 61% |
| Cost per task (API rates) | $14.19 | $1.04 |
| Time per task | 1.5 hours | 15.5 minutes |
| Tokens per task | 27.7M | 3.2M |

Artificial Analysis builds the Coding Agent Index from the three benchmark rows. Claude Code leads on the index and on two of the three benchmarks behind it, Terminal-Bench and SWE-Atlas-QnA. Codex is one point ahead on DeepSWE. Codex finishes each task about six times faster and costs about 14 times less in pay-per-token API terms. Cost per task is an API figure, so it does not reflect what plan subscribers pay. Other setups: Claude Code on Opus 5.5 scored 66, and Codex on GPT-6 Astra scored 62 at $7.47 per task.

### Chat-based coding leaderboards

LMArena's coding boards measure which chat answers voters prefer. On the Text Coding board dated 15 Oct 2026, the previous Claude Fable 5 ranked 2nd at 1551 and Claude Opus 5.5 ranked 6th at 1548. GPT-6 Astra ranked 9th at 1543 and GPT-6.1 Sol 10th at 1540. The current Claude Fable 5.1 ranked 14th at 1537. The best Claude entry and the best OpenAI entry are 8 points apart, which is close to a tie.

The WebDev board (13 Oct 2026) favors Claude more clearly. Claude Opus 5.5 ranked 1st at 1811 and GPT-6 Astra 2nd at 1780, a 31-point gap.

### Vendor claims, kept separate

Anthropic's Opus 5.5 launch post (22 Sep 2026) reported 66.4% on Terminal-Bench 4.0 against 57.9% for GPT-6 Astra, with Opus 5.5 at xhigh effort and Astra at high effort. OpenAI reported the Astra figure, shown inside Anthropic's table. We did not capture OpenAI's own launch table, so treat this as one-sided.

**Where Claude loses:** it costs about 14 times more per task at API rates and takes about six times longer in the Artificial Analysis test. **Where ChatGPT loses:** Codex trails on the index and on two of the three benchmarks, including by 11 points on Terminal-Bench.

**Winner: Claude on quality, ChatGPT on cost and speed.** If budget is tight, Codex scored 63 against 68 at about one fourteenth of the cost per task. For a wider shortlist, see [choosing AI coding tools](https://trutool.co/guides/choosing-ai-coding-tools) and the [AI coding tools](https://trutool.co/categories/ai-coding) category.

## Claude vs ChatGPT for writing and tone: which is better?

There is no independent test that measures writing quality alone, so this one comes down to taste. The nearest independent evidence is the LMArena text leaderboard, where the best Claude entries rank above every OpenAI entry. It covers all text tasks, including writing.

On the 15 Oct 2026 board, Claude Opus 5.5 ranked 3rd (1508), the previous Claude Fable 5 4th (1504) and Claude Fable 5.1 6th (1502). The best-ranked OpenAI entry, GPT-5.6 Sol, ranked 21st (1485), and GPT-6.1 Sol ranked 22nd (1484).

Tone is subjective, and we did not run our own writing tests. Zapier's comparison, dated 14 Oct 2026, calls Claude better for creative work, but that is the reviewer's opinion. The most reliable check is to paste the same brief into both free plans and compare the drafts yourself. More options are listed under [AI writing tools](https://trutool.co/categories/ai-writing).

**Where Claude loses:** it cannot make images to go with your copy. **Where ChatGPT loses:** it ranks lower on general text preference.

**Winner: Claude, narrowly, with low confidence on tone.**

## Which handles long documents better, and how big is the context window?

Claude has the larger context window in the apps. Anthropic lists up to 1M tokens in chat on paid plans for Fable 5.1, Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5 and Haiku 5.5. ChatGPT's pricing page lists 256K tokens for reasoning on Go and Plus and 400K on Pro.

Last checked 16 Oct 2026.

| Limit | Claude | ChatGPT |
|---|---|---|
| Context window in the app | 1M tokens on paid plans for the four current models | Instant: 27K tokens Free, 54K Go and Plus, 128K Pro. Reasoning: 256K tokens Go and Plus, 400K Pro |
| Largest file | 500 MB per file in chat | 512 MB per file |
| Files per chat or period | 20 files per chat | 80 files per 3 hours; 3 per day on Free |
| PDF size | PDFs up to 1,000 pages; visual analysis up to 100 pages | Not stated on the pages we checked |
| Text and document files | Not stated on the pages we checked | Up to 2M tokens per file |
| Image size | Images up to 8000 by 8000 pixels | 20 MB per image |
| Spreadsheet size | Not stated on the pages we checked | About 50 MB per spreadsheet |

Two cautions. ChatGPT's context figures come from a pricing page that lists them under generic "GPT Instant" and "GPT Reasoning" labels with no model names. And a file size limit is a different number from a context window.

**Where Claude loses:** it caps chats at 20 files, while ChatGPT allows 80 files per 3 hours. **Where ChatGPT loses:** a smaller window, from 256K to 400K tokens for reasoning and 27K to 128K for Instant, per its pricing page.

**Winner: Claude for context window size.** ChatGPT accepts more files per period.

## What about images, voice and other extras?

ChatGPT generates images on every plan, including Free, and Claude does not. Anthropic's help center says Claude has no native image generation, though it can build charts, diagrams and HTML or SVG graphics. Both offer voice, web search and deep research. If you are choosing an image tool specifically, see [choosing AI image tools](https://trutool.co/guides/choosing-ai-image-tools). To compare free image limits across ChatGPT, Gemini and other tools, see [best free AI image generators](https://trutool.co/guides/best-free-ai-image-generators).

Last checked 16 Oct 2026.

| Feature | Claude | ChatGPT |
|---|---|---|
| Image generation | No native generation; builds HTML, SVG and charts, plus Claude Design | Yes, ChatGPT Images 2.5, on all plans including Free |
| Voice | Voice mode (beta) on all plans; Fable is not available in voice | Voice mode, with video on Go, Plus and Pro; the newest release-note entry covers GPT-Live-1.1 |
| Deep research | Research, paid plans only, runs on Opus 5.5 | Yes; limits vary by plan |
| Agents | Claude Cowork (now part of Claude chat, rolling out to Pro and Max first), Claude in Chrome | ChatGPT Work (launched 13 Jul 2026, replaced agent mode), workspace agents on Business |
| Projects and apps | Projects (up to 5 on Free), Artifacts, connectors and MCP, Skills | Projects, apps and plugins; new custom GPT creation is closed on personal accounts |

PCMag UK judged ChatGPT's deep research reports deeper in a review updated 23 Aug 2026, before the newest models. That is opinion. OpenAI also removed Canvas from its GPT-5.5 models on 11 Jun 2026, and we could not confirm whether it is back on GPT-6. OpenAI's pricing page still lists custom GPTs for Plus and Pro, which conflicts with the closed-creation note in the table.

**Where Claude loses:** no image generation and voice is labeled beta. **Where ChatGPT loses:** custom GPT creation is closed on personal accounts, agent mode was retired, and the Atlas browser was scheduled to shut down on 9 Aug 2026.

**Winner: ChatGPT for images and voice features.** We did not test voice quality for either.

## Claude AI vs ChatGPT free plans: how do they compare?

Both have a free plan, and neither publishes a fixed message count. Claude Free limits usage by session in five-hour windows. ChatGPT Free promises unlimited everyday text chats subject to abuse safeguards, with separate undisclosed caps on uploads, images, voice and data analysis. ChatGPT Free can show ads in the US.

Last checked 16 Oct 2026.

| Free plan | Claude | ChatGPT |
|---|---|---|
| Message limits | Five-hour session windows, no fixed number | Unlimited everyday text chats; other features capped |
| Models | Sonnet and Haiku models; exact version not stated | A Luna-class model, per the 7 Oct release note |
| Image generation | No | Yes, with undisclosed caps |
| File uploads | Not stated for the Free plan | 3 files per day |
| Ads | Anthropic said on 4 Feb 2026 that Claude will remain ad-free | May show in some countries, including the US |

Anthropic's ad-free line is a company commitment in a blog post, so it could change. OpenAI's help pages say ChatGPT Free and Go may show ads in some countries, including the United States.

**Where Claude loses:** no image generation, and limits are set by session window with no fixed count published. **Where ChatGPT loses:** ads, and a three-file daily upload cap.

**Winner: tie.** ChatGPT Free covers more features, but it can show ads and caps uploads.

## Claude Pro vs ChatGPT Plus: what does each plan cost?

Claude Pro and ChatGPT Plus both cost $20 a month. Claude Pro drops to $17 a month on annual billing, which is $200 paid up front, and ChatGPT Plus has no annual option. ChatGPT also has an $8 Go plan, which may show ads. Higher tiers start at $100 a month on both.


Last checked 16 Oct 2026. All prices are in US dollars before tax. Anthropic notes mobile app-store prices can differ.

| Tier | Claude | ChatGPT |

| Entry paid | None | Go: $8 a month, which may show ads |

On monthly price, Claude Pro and ChatGPT Plus match. The differences are in what the plan includes. Claude Pro includes Claude Code and Research but not Fable 5.1. ChatGPT Plus includes GPT-6 at Medium and High, Codex and image generation, but not Extra High or GPT-6 Pro, which are reserved for Pro, Business and Enterprise.

Neither vendor has a single $200 plan any more. ChatGPT Pro has three listed tiers ($100, $200 and $500) and Claude Max has two ($100 and $200).

**Where Claude loses:** no cheap paid tier, and annual savings need $200 up front. **Where ChatGPT loses:** Go may show ads, and the $17 annual discount has no equivalent.

**Winner: tie at $20 a month.** ChatGPT is cheaper to start with. Claude Pro costs $200 a year against $240 for Plus.

## How do Claude and ChatGPT handle privacy and data use?

ChatGPT personal accounts may use your conversations to improve models unless you turn off "Improve the model for everyone" in Data controls. Claude has a similar "Help improve our AI models" toggle, but we could not confirm which way it is set by default. Business, Team and Enterprise plans do not train on your data by default on either product.

Last checked 16 Oct 2026.

| Question | Claude | ChatGPT |
|---|---|---|
| Used for training? | Not confirmed. A toggle exists, but Anthropic's pages do not state the default | Yes on Free, Go, Plus and Pro unless you turn it off in Data controls |
| Temporary or incognito chats | Incognito chats are never used for training | Temporary Chats are not used for training and are kept up to 30 days for safety |
| Retention if sharing is allowed | De-identified data kept for up to 5 years | Not stated on the pages we checked |
| Work plans | Team and Enterprise: no training by default | Business, Enterprise and Edu: no training by default |

Anthropic's pricing page labels model training as "Opt-out", but the pages we read do not say whether the toggle starts on or off. The one third-party review we read (PCMag UK, updated 23 Aug 2026) says both chatbots train on chats by default, which Anthropic's own pages neither confirm nor deny. Check the toggle in your account settings.

**Where Claude loses:** the default is unclear, and a five-year retention period applies if you allow sharing. **Where ChatGPT loses:** personal plans may use chats for training unless you opt out.

**Winner: no call.** We could not verify Claude's default, so we are not ranking these two.

## Which is better for students?

Both work for students on the free plans. ChatGPT Free adds image generation and voice with caps. Claude Free offers up to 5 Projects. Among paid plans, ChatGPT Go at $8 a month is cheapest, and Claude Pro is $17 a month billed annually.

We did not verify student discounts or education plans for either product, so check both pricing pages before paying. For long readings, Claude's larger context window helps. For slide illustrations, only ChatGPT can create images.

**Where Claude loses:** no images, and no entry-level paid plan. **Where ChatGPT loses:** free uploads are capped at three files a day, and Go may show ads.

**Winner: ChatGPT for the lowest cost, Claude for long readings.**

## Which is better for business and teams?

Teams are priced the same. Claude Team and ChatGPT Business both start at $20 per seat a month on annual billing or $25 monthly, with premium seats at $100 or $125. Neither trains on your data by default.

- **Pick Claude** for long documents, codebases, Claude Code and Cowork. Claude Enterprise also has a self-serve option at $20 per seat a month, billed annually with a 20-seat minimum, plus usage.
- **Pick ChatGPT** for image generation and workspace agents. ChatGPT Business is built for teams of 2 to 200 employees; Claude Team is built for teams of 2 to 150.

**Where Claude loses:** no image generation for marketing or design teams. **Where ChatGPT loses:** agent mode was retired and the Atlas browser was scheduled to shut down on 9 Aug 2026, so workflows built on them need to move to ChatGPT Work.

**Winner: tie.** Price and data defaults match.

## Claude vs ChatGPT vs Gemini: where does Gemini stand?

Gemini currently sits ahead of both on two LMArena boards. As of 15 Oct 2026, Gemini 4 Argon (high) ranked first on the LMArena text board with 1524, marked as a preliminary result. It also ranked first on the Text Coding board at 1559, also preliminary. Claude Opus 5.5 ranked 3rd on the text board at 1508.

Preliminary rankings can move as votes come in. We did not check Gemini's plans or prices, so we do not compare them here. Profile: [Gemini on TruTool](https://trutool.co/tools/gemini).

## Can you use both Claude and ChatGPT?

Yes. A simple split is Claude for long documents, coding and drafting, and ChatGPT for images and voice. Both have free plans, so you can try the split before you pay. If you pay for only one, pick the one that covers your most frequent task.

- Draft or edit long text in Claude, then make cover images or diagrams in ChatGPT.
- Use Claude Code when quality matters and Codex when cost and speed do.

For a method to decide, see [choosing an AI assistant](https://trutool.co/guides/choosing-ai-assistants) and the [AI chatbots](https://trutool.co/categories/ai-chatbots) category.

## What changed recently?

Both lineups changed between February and October 2026. These are the dated changes that affect this comparison, newest first, from each vendor's official pages and release notes.

- **Newest entry, undated on the page:** OpenAI's release notes list GPT-Live-1.1 for voice as the latest update.

## How we compared Claude and ChatGPT

We compared official pricing, help and documentation pages from Anthropic and OpenAI, plus two independent leaderboards, on 16 Oct 2026. We did not run our own benchmarks or writing tests. Vendor claims, opinions and unconfirmed figures are labeled in the text. More on process: [methodology](https://trutool.co/methodology) and [editorial policy](https://trutool.co/editorial-policy).

## Frequently asked questions about Claude vs ChatGPT

### Is Claude better than ChatGPT?

Not across the board. The top Claude models rank higher on the LMArena text board, Claude Code scored higher on coding-agent quality, and Claude has a larger context window. ChatGPT generates images, has an $8 Go plan and offers voice with video. The better choice depends on your main task.

### Is Claude better than ChatGPT for coding?

On quality, yes in one independent test. Artificial Analysis scored Claude Code 68 and Codex 63 on 16 Oct 2026. Codex cost $1.04 per task against $14.19 for Claude Code at API rates. In chat coding rankings on LMArena, the best Claude and OpenAI entries are 8 points apart, which is close to a tie.

### Which is cheaper, Claude Pro or ChatGPT Plus?

Claude Pro and ChatGPT Plus both cost $20 a month. ChatGPT is cheaper to start, with Go at $8 a month, which may show ads. Claude Pro costs $17 a month if you pay $200 a year up front. Higher tiers begin at $100 a month for Claude Max and ChatGPT Pro.

### Can Claude generate images like ChatGPT?

No. Anthropic's help center says Claude has no native image generation. It can build charts, diagrams and HTML or SVG graphics, and it can read images you upload. ChatGPT generates images with ChatGPT Images 2.5 on every plan, including Free, with limits.

### Do Claude and ChatGPT both have a free plan?

Yes. Claude Free and ChatGPT Free both cost $0 and include web search. Neither publishes a fixed message limit. Claude limits usage by five-hour session windows. ChatGPT Free promises unlimited everyday text chats under abuse safeguards, adds image generation with caps, and can show ads in the US.

### Do Claude and ChatGPT use my data for training?

ChatGPT personal plans may use your chats for training unless you turn off "Improve the model for everyone" in Data controls. Claude has a training toggle, but we could not confirm its default. On both, Business, Team and Enterprise plans do not train on your data by default.

### Which has the bigger context window, Claude or ChatGPT?

Claude. Anthropic lists up to 1M tokens in chat on paid plans for its four current models. ChatGPT's pricing page lists 256K tokens for reasoning on Go and Plus and 400K on Pro. ChatGPT's figures are listed under generic Instant and Reasoning labels, so they may change.

### What is the difference between Claude AI and ChatGPT?

Claude AI is made by Anthropic and runs on Fable, Opus, Sonnet and Haiku models. ChatGPT is made by OpenAI and runs mainly on the GPT-6 family (GPT-5.6 Sol is still selectable). The main practical differences are image generation, which only ChatGPT has, and context size, where Claude is larger.

## Quick verdict: is Gemini or ChatGPT better?

Gemini is the better pick for most people paying about $20 monthly, as of 17 Oct 2026; free plans are nearly tied. Google AI Pro's Gemini 4 Argon ranked first, on preliminary scores, on Arena's text and math leaderboards and first but inside the margin of error on coding. ChatGPT is better for web app coding and Office work.

**Last verified 17 Oct 2026.** Prices are US dollars. Benchmarks come from Arena (formerly LMArena) and Artificial Analysis. Feature data: [ChatGPT vs Gemini tool comparison](https://trutool.co/compare/chatgpt-vs-gemini).

- **Everyday chat:** Google Gemini 4 Argon, first on Arena's text board on a preliminary score.
- **Web app coding:** ChatGPT with GPT-6 Astra, second on Arena's WebDev board. Plus includes Astra in Codex and Work.
- **Fewer wrong guesses on a factual test:** Google Gemini 4 Argon at high reasoning, 15% against 51% for GPT-6 Astra at max reasoning.
- **Long documents:** Google Gemini, with a 1M-token context window on Google AI Pro.
- **Video:** Google Gemini, with limited video generation from Google AI Plus. OpenAI discontinued the Sora app on 26 Apr 2026.
- **Word, Excel and PowerPoint:** ChatGPT with GPT-6 Sol, through add-ins with limits on Free and Go.
- **Privacy controls:** ChatGPT, which lets you stop training and keep chat history.

## Gemini vs ChatGPT at a glance: how do they compare?

Gemini is Google's AI assistant and ChatGPT is OpenAI's. Both have a free plan, a plan at about $20 a month and premium tiers from about $100. Gemini wins on context window, video and one hallucination test. ChatGPT wins on web app coding and Office add-ins.

| Category | Google Gemini | OpenAI ChatGPT | Winner |
|---|---|---|---|
| Best chat model on the $20 plan | Gemini 4 Argon on Google AI Pro | GPT-6 Sol on Plus (Astra only in Work and Codex) | Gemini, on available evidence |
| Arena text leaderboard rank, 15 Oct 2026 | 1st, Gemini 4 Argon (preliminary) | 21st, GPT-5.6 Sol | Gemini |
| Arena WebDev leaderboard rank, 16 Oct 2026 | 9th, Gemini 4 Argon (preliminary) | 2nd, GPT-6 Astra; 8th, GPT-6 Sol | ChatGPT |
| Hallucination rate, Artificial Analysis AA-Omniscience test | 15%, Gemini 4 Argon at high reasoning | 51%, GPT-6 Astra at max reasoning | Gemini, on this test |
| Context window | 32K free, 128K Google AI Plus, 1M Google AI Pro and Ultra | 27K free (Instant); Go and Plus 54K (256K when reasoning); Pro 128K (400K when reasoning) | Gemini |
| Video | Limited on Google AI Plus, more on Pro and Ultra | No built-in video generation | Gemini |
| Cheapest paid plan | Google AI Plus, $4.99 a month | Go, $8 a month, may show ads | Gemini |
| Standard plan | Google AI Pro, $19.99 a month | Plus, $20 a month | About the same |
| Office apps | Gmail, Docs and Sheets | Word, Excel, PowerPoint and Google Sheets, with limits on Free and Go | Depends on your suite |
| Training opt-out | Turning it off keeps new chats only 72 hours | Separate toggle, history stays | ChatGPT |

![Comparison table of Gemini and ChatGPT showing the winner in 10 categories as of 17 Oct 2026](/media/8898116e-7ce9-4a60-81aa-289868023a47.webp "1600x1000")

## Which models do Gemini and ChatGPT use in October 2026?

Gemini's top model is Gemini 4 Argon, released to Google AI Pro and Ultra subscribers on 13 Oct 2026. ChatGPT began rolling out GPT-6 on 7 Oct 2026 (Free and Go from 8 Oct), with GPT-6 Sol on Plus and above. See the [Gemini tool profile](https://trutool.co/tools/gemini) and [ChatGPT tool profile](https://trutool.co/tools/chatgpt).

| Plan level | Google Gemini | OpenAI ChatGPT |
|---|---|---|
| Free | A Flash-Lite model | A Luna model |
| Entry | Gemini 3.6 Flash (Google AI Plus) | A Luna model (Go) |
| About $20 | Gemini 4 Argon and Gemini 3.1 Pro (Google AI Pro) | GPT-6 Sol, plus GPT-6 Astra and GPT-6.1 Sol in Work and Codex (Plus) |
| Premium | Gemini 4 Argon with higher limits (Ultra) | GPT-6 Astra in Chat, Work and Codex (Pro) |

OpenAI's pages disagree on the free model: GPT-6 Luna in the 7 Oct release note, GPT-5.6 Luna on the models help page.

OpenAI's release notes call GPT-6 Astra the Pro reasoning option in ChatGPT, while its pricing table marks Astra as available on Plus. Its models help page gives the split: GPT-6 Astra in Chat needs Pro, Business or Enterprise, and Plus includes it in ChatGPT Work and Codex.

## Google Gemini vs ChatGPT: which is better overall?

Gemini is ahead on independent data from mid October 2026, with caveats. Gemini 4 Argon tops Arena's text board on a preliminary score and ties GPT-6 Astra at 53 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index. Gemini includes Argon at $19.99 a month, while ChatGPT's Astra option in Chat needs Pro, Business or Enterprise.

On Arena's text board dated 15 Oct 2026, Gemini 4 Argon (High) is first at 1524 ±9, with a rank spread of 1st to 3rd. GPT-6 Sol, scored at Max effort, which sits above the High setting that is the top Plus level in Chat, is 61st at 1459.

Argon also tops Arena's math board dated 15 Oct 2026, at 1529 ±34 from only 273 votes, and its rank could fall anywhere from 1st to 40th.

On Artificial Analysis's Intelligence Index, Argon cost $1.99 per task at Google's introductory API price, which ends 30 Nov 2026, and $3.98 at the standard price per The Batch, against $3.26 for GPT-6 Astra.

**Where Gemini loses:** Argon is only on Google AI Pro and Ultra, and its scores are preliminary. **Where ChatGPT loses:** Arena has not scored the Plus chat model at the efforts Plus offers.

**Winner: Gemini, at the $20 price point.**

## Gemini vs ChatGPT for coding: which is better?

ChatGPT is better for web app coding and the two are tied on general coding. GPT-6 Astra beats Gemini 4 Argon by 100 points on Arena's WebDev board, and Plus users get Astra only in Codex and Work. On Arena's general coding board, Argon's preliminary lead sits inside the margin of error.

On the Text Coding board dated 15 Oct 2026, Argon is first at 1559 ±17, with a rank spread of 1st to 16th. GPT-6 Astra (Max) is ninth at 1543 ±12.

On the WebDev board dated 16 Oct 2026, GPT-6 Astra (Max) is second at 1778. GPT-6 Sol (Max), the Plus chat model, is level with Argon at 1684 against 1678 ±15.

Arena scored Astra at Max effort, and we could not confirm which efforts Plus gets in Codex. Google lists Argon in Antigravity for Ultra subscribers only.

**Where Gemini loses:** web front ends. **Where ChatGPT loses:** GPT-6 Sol at Max effort, above the top Plus level in Chat, is 39th on the general coding board.

**Winner: ChatGPT for web apps. General coding is a statistical tie on Arena's preference votes.** See [how to choose AI coding tools](https://trutool.co/guides/choosing-ai-coding-tools).

## Gemini vs ChatGPT for writing: which reads better?

Gemini reads better on Arena's creative writing votes, on a preliminary score: on the leaderboard dated 15 Oct 2026, Gemini 4 Argon is second at 1516 ±19, behind Claude Opus 5.5. The best OpenAI entry, GPT-5.6 Sol, is 20th. Tone is a matter of taste, so test both with your own drafts before you pay.

Argon also leads Arena's overall text leaderboard, which covers many task types, so that rank adds little to the writing verdict.

ChatGPT's Word add-in has been available on every plan, including Free, since 23 Sep 2026, with usage limits.

**Where Gemini loses:** help in Gmail starts at Google AI Plus, and Docs needs Google AI Pro. **Where ChatGPT loses:** GPT-6 Sol at Max effort is 61st on the creative writing board.

**Winner: Gemini, on preliminary Arena votes.** More options: [AI writing tools](https://trutool.co/categories/ai-writing).

## Which hallucinates less, Gemini or ChatGPT?

Gemini 4 Argon guessed wrong less often than GPT-6 Astra on one independent factual-recall test. Artificial Analysis's AA-Omniscience benchmark measured a 15% hallucination rate for Argon at high reasoning and 51% for Astra at max reasoning, as reported by DeepLearning.AI's The Batch on 9 Oct 2026.

Artificial Analysis defines the rate as incorrect answers divided by all answers that were not correct, including partial and unattempted ones. The method penalizes wrong answers and does not penalize refusals.

A lower rate can also mean the model refuses more often, so it does not prove better answers overall.

The test compares Argon, on a $19.99 plan, with Astra, which ChatGPT offers in Chat on Pro plans from $100 for individuals, and on Business and Enterprise. We found no figure for GPT-6 Sol, the Plus chat model, and Google does not say which reasoning setting the Gemini app uses. Artificial Analysis showed no per-model values when we checked, so these figures are secondary.

**Winner: Gemini, on this one test.**

## Which handles long documents better, and how big is the context window?

Gemini handles long documents better: Google AI Pro and Ultra give the Gemini app a 1M-token context window, against 256K on ChatGPT Go and Plus and 400K on Pro when ChatGPT is reasoning. Google says 1M tokens is about 1,500 pages or 30,000 lines of code.

Without reasoning, ChatGPT's Instant windows are 27K on Free, 54K on Go and Plus and 128K on Pro. Gemini gives 32K free and 128K on Google AI Plus.

**Winner: Gemini.**

## Gemini vs ChatGPT for images, video and voice: which does more?

Gemini does more than ChatGPT on video: both generate images on their free plans, but only Gemini has built-in video generation, with limited access on Google AI Plus. Free image limits for both, plus eight other tools, are in our [free AI image generator comparison](https://trutool.co/guides/best-free-ai-image-generators). OpenAI discontinued the Sora app and website on 26 Apr 2026, and OpenAI said the Sora API would shut down on 24 Sep 2026.

Gemini makes images with Nano Banana 2 and ChatGPT with ChatGPT Images 2.5, released 11 Sep 2026. Gemini Live is on the free plan, and ChatGPT's voice with video starts at Go.

**Where Gemini loses:** there is no video on the free plan. **Where ChatGPT loses:** there is no built-in video generation on any plan.

**Winner: Gemini.** See [how to choose AI image tools](https://trutool.co/guides/choosing-ai-image-tools).

## Gemini AI vs ChatGPT free plans: what do you get for $0?

Both free plans work for daily use, and neither includes Gemini 4 Argon or GPT-6 Sol. ChatGPT Free promises unlimited everyday text chats under abuse safeguards, but it may show ads. Gemini's free plan runs a Flash-Lite model with a 32K context window and includes Deep Research, Gemini Live and image generation.

ChatGPT ads started in the US in Feb 2026 and have since reached the UK, Canada, Australia and New Zealand. Free users can choose an ad-free option with lower limits.

**Winner: Tie.**

## Gemini vs ChatGPT pricing: which paid plan is better value?

Gemini has the lower list price at the entry level, and the two cost about the same at $20 and $100. As of 17 Oct 2026, Google AI Plus costs $4.99 a month against $8 for ChatGPT Go, and Google AI Pro costs $19.99 against $20 for Plus, with 5 TB of storage.

| Category | Google Gemini | OpenAI ChatGPT | Winner |
|---|---|---|---|
| Free | $0 | $0 | Tie |
| Entry | Google AI Plus, $4.99 a month | Go, $8 a month, may show ads | Gemini |
| Standard | Google AI Pro, $19.99 a month | Plus, $20 a month | About the same |
| Premium | Google AI Ultra, $99.99 or $199.99 a month | Pro, $100, $200 or $500 a month | About the same |
| Teams | Gemini Enterprise Business, from $21 per seat a month, billing term not stated by Google | Business, $25 per user a month billed monthly, or $20 billed annually | Not like for like |

**Where Gemini loses:** limits are stated as multiples, such as 4x on Pro, and depend on prompt complexity. **Where ChatGPT loses:** GPT-6 Astra in Chat needs Pro, Business or Enterprise, and Plus includes it only in ChatGPT Work and Codex.

**Winner: Gemini at the entry level, about the same above it.**

## Which works better with Google Workspace, Microsoft apps and agents?

Gemini fits Google Workspace users better and ChatGPT fits Microsoft Office users better. Gemini works inside Gmail, Docs and Sheets on Google AI Pro and connects to more than 40 apps. ChatGPT has add-ins for Word, Excel, PowerPoint and Google Sheets, with limits on Free and Go, and runs longer jobs in ChatGPT Work.

**Winner: Depends on your suite.** Compare [AI productivity tools](https://trutool.co/categories/ai-productivity).

## How do Gemini and ChatGPT handle privacy and data use?

ChatGPT gives you the cleaner opt-out: you can turn off model training in Data controls and keep your chat history. Gemini uses chats to train Google's models while Keep Activity is on, and turning it off means new chats are kept for only 72 hours. Business plans of both exclude training by default.

| Category | Google Gemini | OpenAI ChatGPT | Winner |
|---|---|---|---|
| Are chats used for training? | Yes, while Keep Activity is on | Yes, unless you turn off "Improve the model for everyone" | ChatGPT |
| Temporary chats | Kept 72 hours and excluded from training | Kept up to 30 days for safety and excluded from training | Tie |
| Ads | Google says chats are not used for ads | Ads on Free and Go in the US, UK, Canada, Australia and New Zealand | Gemini |

On both, sending feedback can put a conversation into training, and Google may still review some chats for safety.

**Winner: ChatGPT for personal accounts.**

## Which is better for students?

The Google Gemini student offer is longer: eligible US college students get 12 months of Google AI Pro free if they redeem by 31 Dec 2026. OpenAI gives eligible US college and graduate students four free months of ChatGPT Plus if they claim by 31 Oct 2026. Both renew at full price unless cancelled.

Both offers need a payment method at sign-up. Eligible students in more than 140 other markets, excluding Canada, get a free year of Google AI Plus.

ChatGPT for Teachers is free for verified US K-12 educators through June 2027.

**Winner: Gemini.** See [AI education tools](https://trutool.co/categories/ai-education).

## Which is better for business and teams?

It depends on your office suite, and the prices are not like for like. Gemini Enterprise Business starts at $21 per seat a month for teams of up to 300, and Google does not state the billing term. ChatGPT Business costs $25 per user a month billed monthly, or $20 billed annually. Neither trains on business data by default.

**Winner: Gemini for Google Workspace teams, ChatGPT for Microsoft 365 teams.**

## Who should pick Gemini and who should pick ChatGPT?

Pick Gemini if you want the strongest chat model on a $20 plan, long-document work, video generation or tight Google Workspace links. Pick ChatGPT if you build web front ends, work in Microsoft Office, want training off with history on, or rely on Codex.

| If you | Pick | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Want the best chat model for about $20 | Gemini | Argon comes with Google AI Pro |
| Build web apps | ChatGPT | GPT-6 Astra is second on WebDev, and Plus gets it in Codex |
| Are a US college student | Gemini | 12 free months of Google AI Pro, against 4 months of ChatGPT Plus |

For a three-way view, read [Claude vs ChatGPT](https://trutool.co/guides/claude-vs-chatgpt) and [Claude vs Gemini](https://trutool.co/compare/claude-vs-gemini), or start with [how to choose an AI assistant](https://trutool.co/guides/choosing-ai-assistants).

## How did we compare Gemini and ChatGPT?

We used vendor pages for prices, models and limits, and two independent sources for performance: Arena's blind-vote leaderboards and Artificial Analysis. We did not run our own benchmark for this guide. Every fact was checked on 17 Oct 2026, and we update the page when either company changes its plans or models.

Read our [methodology](https://trutool.co/methodology) and [editorial policy](https://trutool.co/editorial-policy), or see [ChatGPT alternatives](https://trutool.co/alternatives/chatgpt), [Gemini alternatives](https://trutool.co/alternatives/gemini) and [AI chatbots](https://trutool.co/categories/ai-chatbots).

## What do people ask about Gemini vs ChatGPT?

These are the main questions to settle when you compare Gemini and ChatGPT. Each answer stands on its own and draws on the vendor pages and leaderboards named in this guide. Prices are in US dollars, checked on 17 Oct 2026, so recheck plan details before you buy.

### Is Gemini better than ChatGPT?

For most people who pay about $20 a month, yes, as of 17 Oct 2026. Gemini 4 Argon, included with Google AI Pro at $19.99, ranks first on Arena's text board on a preliminary score. On the free plans it is closer to a tie. ChatGPT is better for web app coding and for Word, Excel and PowerPoint work.

### Is Google Gemini free?

Yes. Gemini's free plan costs $0 and includes a Flash-Lite model, image generation, Deep Research, Gemini Live and Canvas, with a 32K-token context window. Limits refresh every five hours up to a weekly cap. Gemini 4 Argon, Google's newest model, needs Google AI Pro at $19.99 a month or Ultra.

### Is ChatGPT free?

Yes. ChatGPT Free costs $0 and includes unlimited everyday text chats under abuse safeguards, plus limited uploads, image creation, voice chats and deep research. It runs a Luna model and may show ads in the US, UK, Canada, Australia and New Zealand, with an ad-free option that has lower limits. GPT-6 Sol needs Plus at $20 a month.

### Which is cheaper, Google AI Pro or ChatGPT Plus?

They cost almost the same. Google AI Pro is $19.99 a month and ChatGPT Plus is $20 a month, as of 17 Oct 2026. Google AI Pro adds 5 TB of storage. At the entry level, Google AI Plus costs $4.99 a month and ChatGPT Go costs $8 and may show ads.

### Is Gemini or ChatGPT better for coding?

ChatGPT is better for web app coding and the two are tied on general coding. Gemini 4 Argon is first on Arena's general coding board on a preliminary score, and GPT-6 Astra is ninth, within the margin of error. On Arena's WebDev board, Astra is second and Argon ninth. ChatGPT Plus includes Astra in Codex.

### Can ChatGPT make videos like Gemini?

No. ChatGPT has no built-in video generation. OpenAI discontinued the Sora app and website on 26 Apr 2026, and OpenAI said the Sora API would shut down on 24 Sep 2026. Gemini generates video on Google AI Plus, with limited access, and on Pro and Ultra. Both assistants generate images on their free plans.

### Does Gemini use my chats to train its models?

Yes, while Keep Activity is on. Google says human reviewers see a subset of chats, and reviewed chats are kept up to three years without your account details. With Keep Activity off, chats are kept 72 hours and not used for training unless you send feedback. ChatGPT offers a separate training toggle in Data controls.

### Which hallucinates less, Gemini or ChatGPT?

Gemini 4 Argon had a lower hallucination rate than GPT-6 Astra on one independent test, 15% vs 51%, with Argon at high reasoning and Astra at max reasoning. The figures come from Artificial Analysis's AA-Omniscience test, as reported by The Batch on 9 Oct 2026. A lower rate can also reflect more refusals.

### Is Gemini or ChatGPT better for students?

Gemini has the longer student offer. Google gives eligible US college students 12 months of Google AI Pro free if they redeem by 31 Dec 2026, then $19.99 a month unless cancelled. OpenAI offers eligible US college students four free months of ChatGPT Plus if they claim it by 31 Oct 2026, then $20 a month.

## Quick verdict: what is the best free AI image generator in 2026?

The best free AI image generator depends on what you need, and only some vendors publish a number. Gemini and ChatGPT suit people already in a chat assistant, but publish no image limit. Bing Image Creator, Ideogram, Leonardo and Krea publish fixed allowances, each in its own unit. We read every vendor page on 19 Oct 2026.

**Last verified 19 Oct 2026.** Next check: by 19 Nov 2026. Limits come from vendor pages; we ran no image tests, so this guide makes no quality claims.

- **You already use a chat assistant:** Gemini, ChatGPT and Grok include free image creation; Gemini also states its refresh rule, every 5 hours up to a weekly limit.
- **You want a known daily number:** Bing Image Creator gives 15 free fast creations a day, then standard speed.
- **You plan to use the images commercially:** Ideogram and Adobe say commercial use is allowed and name no plan condition, Adobe for non-beta features only; Leonardo grants a licence but keeps the rights; Playground a royalty-free licence. Recraft's free images are not licensed for commercial use.
- **You want a stated no-card sign-up:** Only Krea's pricing page states "No credit card required"; the others are silent on cards.
- **You work in Adobe apps:** Adobe Firefly gives a limited number of free daily generations.

## How do the free AI image generators compare at a glance?

Ten tools have a free image plan confirmed on the vendor's own page as of 19 Oct 2026. Five publish no number: Gemini, ChatGPT, Grok, Adobe Firefly and Recraft. Four count in fast creations, credits, Fast Tokens or units. Playground also publishes a number, but its page gives two. Rows follow no ranking.

| Tool and source | Free allowance, in the vendor's unit | Commercial use on free | Main catch |
|---|---|---|---|

| [Adobe Firefly](https://helpx.adobe.com/firefly/get-set-up/learn-the-basics/generative-credits-faq.html), Adobe apps | "A limited number of free daily generations"; no number published | Allowed for features without the beta label; names no plan condition | Page mixes daily and monthly wording |

Tool names link to the vendor page read on 19 Oct 2026. Units differ, so the numbers cannot be compared across rows. "Not stated" marks a gap in the page we read, and the feature may still exist.

## What does Gemini give you for free?

Gemini gives free users image generation and editing, according to [Google's subscriptions page](https://gemini.google/subscriptions/). Google's [usage limits page](https://support.google.com/gemini/answer/16275805) gives no number: free limits are compute-based, refresh every 5 hours until you reach a weekly limit, and can change without notice. You must sign in with a Google account, and free downloads are 1K resolution.

Google's [image help page](https://support.google.com/gemini/answer/14286560) says downloads at 2K and redoing an image with Nano Banana Pro need a paid Google AI plan.

**Main catch:** no fixed daily number to plan around.

See the [Gemini profile](https://trutool.co/tools/gemini), [Gemini alternatives](https://trutool.co/alternatives/gemini), or our [Gemini vs ChatGPT guide](https://trutool.co/guides/gemini-vs-chatgpt).

## What does ChatGPT give you for free?

ChatGPT's free plan includes image creation, which [OpenAI's pricing page](https://openai.com/chatgpt/pricing/) lists as "Limited image creation" with no number. OpenAI's [help page](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/11084440) says ChatGPT Images is available on all tiers and names the model ChatGPT Images 2.5. Pro lists "Unlimited and faster image creation", and images with thinking is available on Plus, Pro and Business.

OpenAI's pricing and help pages state no watermark or sign-in rule. Its Terms of Use, effective 1 Jan 2026, say that as between you and OpenAI you own the Output.

**Main catch:** no published number; counts in other guides are estimates.

See the [ChatGPT profile](https://trutool.co/tools/chatgpt) and [ChatGPT alternatives](https://trutool.co/alternatives/chatgpt).

## What does Grok give you for free?

Grok's free plan costs $0 and lists Imagine image generation as "Limited" on [xAI's pricing page](https://x.ai/pricing), with no number. Free usage draws on a pool that refreshes weekly, so once it runs out you wait for the next weekly reset. Video generation is not part of the free plan.

Grok's terms, updated 12 Oct 2026, say you keep ownership rights to User Content, which includes Output, and that when using Output you must attribute your generation of it to the service under its brand guidelines.

**Main catch:** no published number, plus attribution rules for Output.

See the [Grok profile](https://trutool.co/tools/grok) and [Grok alternatives](https://trutool.co/alternatives/grok).

## What does Bing Image Creator give you for free?

Bing Image Creator gives 15 free fast creations per day with a personal Microsoft account, then switches to standard speed automatically, according to [Microsoft's feature page](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/bing/features/bing-image-creator). You can top up fast creations with Microsoft Rewards points. Work and school accounts on Microsoft Entra ID cannot use it.

Each image carries a watermark in the bottom left corner plus C2PA content credentials, and Microsoft stores images for up to 90 days. The Image Creator terms, updated March 2026, say Microsoft does not claim ownership of Creations and that the service is for entertainment purposes.

**Main catch:** a watermark on every image.

See the [Bing Image Creator profile](https://trutool.co/tools/bing-image-creator) and [Bing Image Creator alternatives](https://trutool.co/alternatives/bing-image-creator).

## What does Adobe Firefly give you for free?

Adobe Firefly's free plan gives "a limited number of free daily generations" across generative features on a curated set of models, per [Adobe's credits FAQ](https://helpx.adobe.com/firefly/get-set-up/learn-the-basics/generative-credits-faq.html), updated 30 Sep 2026. Adobe publishes no number and says the count, features and models may change. You need an Adobe account.

The same FAQ says free-plan credits expire one month after allocation, so the page mixes daily and monthly wording. Adobe lists Firefly Image 5 at 10 credits per generation and Image 4 Ultra at 20 as premium features, and gives free plans "Limited complimentary generations" of premium features.

Adobe says non-beta outputs can be used commercially, with no plan named. For partner models, the [text to image page](https://www.adobe.com/products/firefly/features/text-to-image.html) says you judge whether the output suits your project.

**Main catch:** no published daily number.

See the [Adobe Firefly profile](https://trutool.co/tools/adobe-firefly) and [Adobe Firefly alternatives](https://trutool.co/alternatives/adobe-firefly).

## What does Ideogram give you for free?

Ideogram gives free accounts 30 credits each week, but only when you sign in with Google, Apple or Microsoft, according to its [plans documentation](https://docs.ideogram.ai/plans-and-billing/available-plans), last verified by Ideogram on 15 Oct 2026. Accounts made with an email and password get no free credits, and the pricing FAQ says the weekly amount may vary.

Everything you generate on the free plan is public, and Plus and Pro plans can unpublish images. Editing and Image Reference need priority credits.

Ideogram's [pricing FAQ](https://ideogram.ai/pricing) says it does not claim ownership and that "you're free to use them for any purpose, including commercial use." It names no plan condition.

**Main catch:** free images are public, and email sign-ups get nothing.

See the [Ideogram profile](https://trutool.co/tools/ideogram) and [Ideogram alternatives](https://trutool.co/alternatives/ideogram).

## What does Leonardo AI give you for free?

Leonardo's free plan gives 150 Fast Tokens per day, with Basic quality and one collection, per its [pricing page](https://www.leonardo.ai/pricing). A token does not map to a fixed number of images, because cost varies by action, and third-party models such as Nano Banana always consume tokens.

Free creations are public. On the free plan Leonardo holds the rights and gives you a non-exclusive, royalty-free licence for commercial use.

**Main catch:** public images, and Leonardo keeps the rights.

See the [Leonardo AI profile](https://trutool.co/tools/leonardo-ai) and [Leonardo AI alternatives](https://trutool.co/alternatives/leonardo-ai).

## What does Krea give you for free?

Krea's free plan gives 100 units per day at $0, and its [pricing page](https://www.krea.ai/pricing) states "No credit card required", the only pricing page here to say so. Units buy different counts per model: the table lists 50 a day on Krea 2 Turbo, about 30 on Flux.1 Dev, about 18 on Krea 1 and about 5 on Krea 3 Beta.

The free plan runs one image at a time and includes limited upscaling up to 2K.

Krea's FAQ lists a commercial license for its paid plans, and the Free plan card does not list it.

**Main catch:** no commercial licence on free images.

See the [Krea profile](https://trutool.co/tools/krea) and [Krea alternatives](https://trutool.co/alternatives/krea).

## What does Playground give you for free?

Playground's [pricing page](https://playground.com/pricing) contradicts itself on the free limit. One line says "Create up to 10 images every 3 hours", while the plan table lists 5 images per 3-hour rolling window. Both sit beside 3 monthly generations across Muse Image, Nano Banana, GPT Image 2, GPT Image 2.5 and Seedream, and 2 downloads per day.

The free plan lists a world-wide royalty free licence. Playground says free generation is slower at peak times, and its FAQ does not allow multiple accounts.

**Main catch:** conflicting limits, 3 monthly generations and 2 downloads a day.

See the [Playground profile](https://trutool.co/tools/playground) and [Playground alternatives](https://trutool.co/alternatives/playground).

## What does Recraft give you for free?

Recraft's free plan offers limited credits for image and vector generation, with no credit number on the pages we read. Each prompt makes up to two images, you can upload up to three images per day, and credit top-ups are only available on paid plans, per Recraft's [free plan documentation](https://www.recraft.ai/docs/plans-and-billing/free-plan).

Free images are public and may appear in Recraft's community gallery. Recraft's [pricing FAQ](https://www.recraft.ai/pricing) says it owns free images and does not license them for commercial use.

**Main catch:** free output is public and not licensed for commercial use.

See the [Recraft profile](https://trutool.co/tools/recraft) and [Recraft alternatives](https://trutool.co/alternatives/recraft).

## Which free AI image generators need a credit card or a specific sign-in?

Only Krea's pricing page says "No credit card required". The other nine list a free plan but state no card rule on the pages we read. Sign-in rules are stated for four: a Google account for Gemini, a personal Microsoft account for Bing, an Adobe account for Firefly, and Google, Apple or Microsoft for Ideogram's credits.

## Can you use free AI images commercially?

It depends on the tool. Leonardo grants a royalty-free commercial licence on its free plan but keeps the rights, and Playground lists a royalty-free licence. Ideogram and Adobe allow commercial use and name no plan condition, Adobe only for non-beta features. Recraft does not license free images for commercial use, and Krea lists a licence only on paid plans.

Ownership terms from [OpenAI](https://openai.com/policies/terms-of-use/), [Grok](https://x.ai/legal/terms-of-service) and [Microsoft](https://www.bing.com/new/termsofuseimagecreator) are in the comparison table above. Before client work, use our [checklist for using AI images in client work](https://trutool.co/community/ai-image-commercial-checks).

## Which free plans add a watermark or make your images public?

Bing Image Creator is the only tool here whose page states a watermark, in the bottom left corner of every image, plus C2PA content credentials. Ideogram, Leonardo and Recraft make free images public. The other vendor pages we read do not state a watermark for free images. The table below collects both.

| Tool | Watermark on free images | Free images public |
|---|---|---|
| Bing Image Creator | Yes, bottom left, plus C2PA | Not stated |
| Ideogram | Not stated | Yes |
| Leonardo AI | Not stated | Yes |
| Recraft | Not stated | Yes, may appear in its gallery |
| The other six | Not stated | Not stated |

## How did we check these free limits?

We read each vendor's own pricing, plan, help or terms page on 19 Oct 2026 and recorded each free allowance in its own unit, with its source. We ran no image or sign-up tests, so the guide makes no claims about image quality or sign-up screens.

Pages were read from India, and plans can differ by country. This page covers free limits only. If you want the best image generating AI for paid work, see [how to choose AI image tools](https://trutool.co/guides/choosing-ai-image-tools) for quality and licence checks, or browse the [AI image tools category](https://trutool.co/categories/ai-image).

Many lists of the best AI image generator free options quote Firefly and Playground figures that vendor pages do not show as free allowances. We left out Canva and Meta AI because their pages did not confirm a free image limit.

## What do people ask about free AI image generators?

These are the questions to settle before you pick a free AI image generator. Each answer stands on its own and uses the vendor pages named in this guide, checked 19 Oct 2026. Free tiers change, so recheck before a big project.

### What is the best free AI image generator in 2026?

As of 19 Oct 2026, it depends on what you need. Gemini and ChatGPT list free image creation inside a chat assistant but publish no number, and Google says Gemini limits can change without notice. Bing Image Creator, Ideogram, Leonardo and Krea publish fixed allowances, each in its own unit, so you can plan around them.

### Which free AI image generator has the highest daily limit?

As of 19 Oct 2026, no single winner exists, because vendors count in different units. Leonardo gives 150 Fast Tokens a day, Krea gives 100 units a day and Bing gives 15 fast creations a day. Gemini, ChatGPT, Grok, Firefly and Recraft publish no number. Units are not interchangeable, so one ranking figure would mislead.

### Is there an unlimited free AI image generator?

As of 19 Oct 2026, none of the ten vendor pages we read says its free image plan is unlimited. Five publish no number and five publish a limit in their own unit. ChatGPT's pricing page lists unlimited image creation only for Pro. Free limits can change, so check the vendor page before a big batch.

### Is the Gemini image generator free?

As of 19 Oct 2026, yes. Google's subscription page lists image generation and editing in the free plan. Free limits are compute-based, refresh every five hours until a weekly cap, and Google says they can change without notice. Free downloads are 1K resolution, while 2K needs a Google AI plan.

### How many free images can you make in ChatGPT?

As of 19 Oct 2026, OpenAI publishes no number. Its pricing page lists limited image creation on the free plan and unlimited image creation on Pro. Treat any figure you see elsewhere as an estimate, and recheck the pricing page before a large batch.

### Does Bing Image Creator cost anything?

As of 19 Oct 2026, no. Microsoft says it is free with a personal Microsoft account and gives 15 free fast creations a day, then continues at standard speed. Each image carries a watermark in the bottom left corner plus content credentials. Work and school accounts cannot use it.

### Do free AI image generators allow commercial use?

As of 19 Oct 2026, it depends on the tool. Leonardo grants a commercial licence on the free plan but keeps the rights. Recraft says free images are not licensed for commercial use. Krea lists a commercial licence only on paid plans. Playground states a royalty-free licence. For ChatGPT, Grok, Bing and Gemini, read the vendor's terms before publishing.

### Which free AI image generators make your images public?

As of 19 Oct 2026, Ideogram says everything generated on its free plan is public. Leonardo lists free creations as Public, and Recraft says free images are public and may appear in its community gallery. Paid plans on all three add private or unpublished images.

### Do you need a credit card for a free AI image generator?

As of 19 Oct 2026, Krea's pricing page states that no credit card is required for its free plan. The other nine vendors in this guide list a free plan, and the pages we read do not say whether a card is asked for. Ideogram gives free credits only to accounts that sign in with Google, Apple or Microsoft.

### Is there a free AI image generator with no sign-up?

As of 19 Oct 2026, none of the ten vendor pages we read says you can generate images without an account. Gemini, Bing, Firefly and Ideogram name an account type, and Microsoft's terms say unauthenticated users cannot generate Creations. The other pages do not say, and we did not check tools outside this list.

### Why do free limits differ between guides?

Vendors change free tiers often and count in tokens, credits, units or images. Several guides quote a monthly Firefly credit figure, but Adobe's help page, updated 30 September 2026, says free users get a limited number of daily generations and gives no number. This guide dates each figure to its source.

body:
The best Sociabble alternatives in 2026 are Haiilo, HubEngage and Staffbase for teams that need communication and engagement in one place, and EveryoneSocial or DSMN8 for teams that mainly want employees sharing brand content on social media. Firstup and Simpplr suit large enterprises that want AI targeting or a full intranet.

Poppulo acquired Sociabble in May 2026, and the product now runs as the Poppulo Experience Platform ([Poppulo release, 26 May 2026](https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/05/26/3301034/0/en/poppulo-acquires-sociabble-to-power-its-employee-experience-platform-for-communications-and-business-leaders-in-the-era-of-agentic-work.html)). Poppulo says existing customers keep the same login, data and success team, and the platform adds email, newsletters, Microsoft Teams and digital signage channels ([Poppulo](https://www.poppulo.com/sociabble)).

That change is a natural moment to review the market. This guide compares seven internal communication platforms and employee advocacy tools on advocacy depth, frontline reach, pricing visibility and fit, using vendor sites and public review data checked in October 2026.

## Quick picks: the best Sociabble alternatives by buyer type

- **Haiilo:** best overall match if you use Sociabble for both internal comms and employee advocacy.
- **HubEngage:** best for frontline and multichannel engagement with gamification across the whole platform.
- **Staffbase:** best for large enterprises that want an intranet, employee app, email and signage from one vendor.
- **EveryoneSocial:** best for dedicated, large-scale employee advocacy programs with governance needs.
- **DSMN8:** best for marketing-led advocacy programs that want modular add-ons.
- **Firstup:** best for AI-driven targeting of critical messages to frontline staff.
- **Simpplr:** best for knowledge workers who want an AI intranet with search and recognition.

![Quick picks of seven Sociabble alternatives, each with the buyer it suits best](/media/d7449a26-4790-4f83-832f-bbb4e2ff7fb3.webp "1600x1200")

## How do the 7 alternatives compare?

![Table comparing seven Sociabble alternatives on best fit, strength, public pricing and free trial](/media/e9f2e26a-b3cb-4754-84e1-0ce21ed97a58.webp "1600x1400")

| Tool | Best for | Advocacy vs comms strength | Pricing (public?) | Free trial |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Haiilo | Comms plus advocacy in one suite | Balanced; full suite quote only | Advocacy from $15 per seat per month (seat minimum shown as 100 and 150; confirm in quote); intranet on quote | Demo only |
| HubEngage | Frontline, multichannel engagement | Comms and engagement first; advocacy via Social Hub | Pricing on request | Demo only |
| Staffbase | Enterprise intranet and employee app | Comms first | Pricing on request (frontline pricing offered) | Demo only |
| EveryoneSocial | Enterprise advocacy at scale | Advocacy first | Pricing on request (priced by users) | Demo only |
| DSMN8 | Marketing-led advocacy | Advocacy first | Pricing on request | Demo only |
| Firstup | AI-targeted frontline messaging | Comms first | Pricing on request (per user, annual commitment) | Demo only |
| Simpplr | AI intranet for desk teams | Comms first | Pricing on request | Demo only |

None of the seven vendors showed a self-serve free trial on its website when checked in October 2026. "Demo only" means a sales-led demo is the published route.

## Why do teams switch from Sociabble?

Teams usually start looking at Sociabble alternatives when the platform feels heavier than the program they run. G2's AI summary of Sociabble reviews names a high volume of posts and a complex admin architecture as the main friction points.

On [G2](https://ai.g2.com/product/sociabble), Sociabble holds a 4.7 out of 5 rating from 416 reviews as of October 2026. The same summary says users like the ease of use and the training on offer.

The move to Poppulo adds more channels, which suits some teams and adds weight for others. Buyers who mainly want employee advocacy, or a lighter frontline app, often use a change of ownership to reopen the shortlist.

## How much does Sociabble cost in 2026?

Sociabble pricing is not published. The old Sociabble pricing URL now redirects to [Poppulo's Sociabble page](https://www.poppulo.com/sociabble), which offers a demo request and no prices, and [G2](https://ai.g2.com/product/sociabble) lists the product as custom pricing.

That makes like for like comparison hard. Of the seven alternatives below, only Haiilo publishes a starting price for advocacy. Everyone else quotes on request, so plan for demos with two or three shortlisted vendors.

## 1. Haiilo: which alternative covers both comms and advocacy?

Haiilo is the closest overall match for most Sociabble customers. It sells an AI intranet and employee app alongside a dedicated employee advocacy product, so one vendor can cover internal news and external sharing, which is how many teams use Sociabble today.

**Strengths**

- Separate plans for intranet and advocacy, so you can buy one or both ([Haiilo pricing](https://haiilo.com/pricing)).
- Advocacy Starter is listed from $15 per seat per month, with web and mobile apps, instant social sharing, analytics and email digests.
- Higher advocacy tiers add Smart Share timing, UTM tagging and LinkedIn impressions analytics.
- Use cases include frontline workers, employer branding and talent acquisition ([Haiilo](https://haiilo.com)).

**Weakness**

- Haiilo's pricing page shows a 100 seat minimum on the Starter card, and its FAQ cites 150, so confirm the minimum in your quote. Intranet plans and higher advocacy tiers are quote only.

**Best for:** teams replacing Sociabble feature for feature, with a balanced need for internal comms and advocacy.

## 2. HubEngage: which alternative is best for frontline and multichannel engagement?

HubEngage is the best fit when your Sociabble use is mostly about reaching and engaging employees, especially frontline teams. Its homepage lists delivery over SMS, push alerts, email, its intranet and mobile apps, plus Slack, Microsoft Teams and signage screens, and it gamifies participation across the whole platform ([HubEngage](https://www.hubengage.com/)).

HubEngage ranks second because it matches the frontline reach and gamification that many Sociabble customers value. Its advocacy is lighter than Haiilo's, which keeps it behind the top pick for advocacy-heavy programs.

It ranks ahead of Staffbase on this page's criteria because it offers native SMS, platform-wide gamification and modular entry, while Staffbase lists no advocacy product.

**Strengths**

- Modular "Hubs" for communications, recognition, social, surveys and forms, and messaging, so you can start with one and add more.
- Channel reach includes iOS and Android apps, web, internal email, SMS, Slack, Microsoft Teams and digital displays, with content auto-formatted for each channel.
- Gamification with points, badges and leaderboards when employees read posts, confirm messages, answer surveys or thank colleagues.
- The [Social Hub](https://www.hubengage.com/software/employee-social-hub/) lists sentiment analysis, auto translation in 14+ languages and the option to bring in external users such as vendors and partners.
- The same page says monthly, annual and multi-year contracts are available.

**Weakness**

- HubEngage does not publish a dedicated external employee advocacy product with social sharing analytics like EveryoneSocial or DSMN8 do. If LinkedIn amplification is your main KPI, check that workflow closely in the demo.

**Best for:** HR and internal comms teams with frontline or deskless staff who want one employee communication platform for news, recognition, surveys and messaging.

## 3. Staffbase: which alternative suits a large enterprise intranet?

Staffbase is a strong option for large organizations that want a mature intranet, a branded employee app and internal email from one vendor. It also offers digital signage, audio briefings and live town halls, and it publishes dedicated frontline pricing.

**Strengths**

- Broad channel set: intranet, Superapp, email, headless CMS, digital signage, On Air audio and Live town halls ([Staffbase](https://staffbase.com)).
- Frontline-specific pricing, so deskless staff only pay for what they need ([Staffbase pricing](https://staffbase.com/pricing)).
- Integrations with Microsoft, ServiceNow, Cornerstone and Google.
- Staffbase's homepage puts its enterprise customer count above 1,500.

**Weakness**

- Staffbase did not list an employee advocacy product in its main platform menu when checked in October 2026, so teams that rely on Sociabble's social sharing would need a second tool.

**Best for:** enterprises consolidating intranet, app and email, where advocacy is secondary.

## 4. EveryoneSocial: which alternative is strongest for advocacy at scale?

EveryoneSocial is the pick for organizations whose main Sociabble use case is employee advocacy. It focuses on getting employees and executives to share content, and adds brand page analytics plus compliance controls for regulated sectors.

**Strengths**

- Dedicated products for employee advocacy, executive activation, company page insights and governance ([EveryoneSocial](https://everyonesocial.com)).
- One plan priced by number of users, covering pilots of 500 people up to rollouts of 50,000+ ([EveryoneSocial pricing](https://everyonesocial.com/pricing/)).
- SOC 2, SSO and SCIM are standard on every plan, with a named success manager.

**Weakness**

- It is an advocacy specialist, so you would still need a separate intranet or employee app for internal news, and pricing is quote only.

**Best for:** marketing, sales and comms teams running a large or regulated advocacy program.

## 5. DSMN8: which alternative is best for marketing-led advocacy?

DSMN8 is a dedicated employee advocacy platform with modular add-ons. It suits marketing teams that want to grow brand reach through employees and pick modules such as executive influence, boosted posts and newsletters.

**Strengths**

- Unlimited admin seats and onboarding are listed as included in every package ([DSMN8 pricing](https://dsmn8.com/pricing/)).
- Live in-platform chat support.
- Integrations with Slack, Microsoft Teams, Adobe Analytics, Salesforce and Marketo.

**Weakness**

- DSMN8 says contracts are annual and the price depends on seats and modules, so small pilots carry a year-long commitment. Ask for a written quote.

**Best for:** marketing-led advocacy programs that want to add modules over time.

## 6. Firstup: which alternative uses AI to target frontline messages?

Firstup is an intelligent communication platform built to get each message to the employees it is meant for, including hard-to-reach frontline staff. It focuses on turning critical communications such as safety updates into completed actions ([Firstup](https://firstup.io)).

**Strengths**

- AI that drafts campaigns and picks the audience for each one.
- AI Search that answers employee questions.
- Engagement and compliance tracking for safety and operational messages.

**Weakness**

- Firstup does not market an employee advocacy product, and its [pricing page](https://firstup.io/pricing/) says plans are priced per user on annual commitments, with quotes only on request.

**Best for:** large operational workforces in healthcare, retail and manufacturing that need reliable, targeted messaging.

## 7. Simpplr: which alternative is best for an AI intranet?

Simpplr is an AI intranet and employee experience platform for organizations that want enterprise search, newsletters, surveys and recognition in one place. It works best for desk-based and hybrid teams that need a knowledge hub ([Simpplr](https://www.simpplr.com)).

**Strengths**

- Intranet, multichannel comms, AI newsletter and enterprise search in one product.
- Surveys, recognition and rewards, and analytics.
- Subscriptions include technical support, customer success oversight and training ([Simpplr pricing](https://www.simpplr.com/pricing/)).

**Weakness**

- Simpplr did not list a dedicated employee advocacy module on its platform menu when checked in October 2026, and its quote model keeps cost unknown until a sales call.

**Best for:** companies replacing an aging intranet that care more about knowledge access than social sharing.

## How should you choose between these Sociabble alternatives?

Start with your main use case. If your Sociabble program is half internal comms and half advocacy, Haiilo is the closest swap. If it is mainly frontline engagement, shortlist HubEngage and Staffbase.

If advocacy is the core goal, compare EveryoneSocial and DSMN8, the two dedicated employee advocacy platforms on this list, side by side. Ask each vendor for share rates and reach analytics from a pilot.

Check frontline access. Sociabble lets frontline workers log in without a corporate email, so confirm each shortlisted tool handles deskless sign-in, SMS or kiosk access.

Count channels. List the channels you use today, such as Teams, email, signage and SMS, and confirm each one is native. Our guide to [choosing team communication tools](https://trutool.co/guides/choosing-team-communication-tools) covers the wider category.

Ask for written quotes. With Haiilo's advocacy plan as the only public price, request per-seat pricing, minimum seats and contract length in writing.

## FAQ

### What are the best Sociabble alternatives?

The best Sociabble alternatives are Haiilo for combined comms and advocacy, HubEngage for frontline multichannel engagement, and Staffbase for enterprise intranets. EveryoneSocial and DSMN8 lead for pure advocacy, while Firstup and Simpplr fit large enterprises focused on AI messaging or intranet search.

### Is Sociabble still available after the Poppulo acquisition?

Yes. Poppulo acquired Sociabble in May 2026 and now sells it as the Poppulo Experience Platform. Poppulo says existing logins, data, roadmap and customer success teams stay the same.

### How much does Sociabble cost?

Sociabble does not publish pricing. Its old pricing URL redirects to a Poppulo page with a demo request, and G2 lists custom pricing. Among the alternatives, Haiilo lists advocacy from $15 per seat per month, with a seat minimum shown as 100 on its pricing card and 150 in its FAQ.

### What is the best Sociabble alternative for employee advocacy software?

EveryoneSocial and DSMN8 are the strongest choices if you want employee advocacy software focused only on social sharing. Haiilo is the best pick if you also need an intranet, since it sells both products.

### Which Sociabble alternative works best for frontline employees?

HubEngage and Staffbase are the strongest for frontline teams. HubEngage reaches staff through an app, SMS, email, Microsoft Teams, Slack and digital signage with gamification, while Staffbase offers frontline-specific pricing and a branded Superapp.

### Do any Sociabble alternatives offer a free trial?

None of the seven vendors showed a self-serve free trial on its website in October 2026. Each one offers a sales-led demo, and EveryoneSocial mentions pilots starting at 500 people.
