body:
AI RFP software, also called AI RFP response software, reads an incoming RFP, RFI, DDQ or security questionnaire, finds approved answers in your company knowledge, drafts a cited response to each question and routes uncertain items to human reviewers.

We compared seven of the best AI RFP software options for 2026. AutoRFP.ai ranks first for its published pricing and cited answers, and Responsive second for large enterprise teams. Inventive AI ranks third and is the strongest pick for RFPs plus security questionnaires with cited answers from scattered knowledge. Loopio, Arphie, SiftHub and Conveyor follow, each with a clear fit and one real weakness.

## Types of RFP software

- **AI-native response platforms.** Built around retrieval and cited drafting. Inventive AI, AutoRFP.ai, Arphie and SiftHub fit here.
- **Library-led response management platforms.** Built around a governed Q&A library and project workflow, now with AI drafting. Loopio and Responsive fit here.
- **Security and trust specialists.** Focused on security questionnaires and trust centers, with RFP support. Conveyor fits here.
- **Proposal builders.** Tools for designed sales proposals and quotes. These are a different category, and we left them out of this list.

## Key features of AI RFP software

Look for these capabilities when you compare tools, and use them as a checklist during a pilot.

- **Cited answers.** Each draft links to the document or past response it came from.
- **Confidence signals.** Low-confidence drafts are marked so reviewers check them first.
- **Live knowledge sync.** Content flows in from SharePoint, Google Drive, Notion, Confluence or similar systems.
- **Stale content detection.** The tool flags outdated or conflicting answers in the library.
- **Format handling.** It works directly in Word, Excel, PDF files and procurement portals.
- **Review routing.** Questions go to the right subject matter expert, often through Slack or Microsoft Teams.
- **Requirements checks.** Agents compare draft answers against the buyer's requirements before submission.
- **Security questionnaire support.** RFPs, DDQs and security questionnaires run in one workflow.

## How does AI RFP response software work?

Most AI RFP response software follows the same five steps:

1. **Intake.** You upload the buyer's Word, Excel or PDF file, or connect a procurement portal. The tool extracts each question and requirement.
2. **Retrieval.** It searches your approved content: past responses, a Q&A library, and connected sources such as SharePoint, Google Drive, Notion or Confluence.
3. **Drafting.** A language model writes an answer for each question from the retrieved material and links the sources it used.
4. **Review.** Low-confidence or sensitive answers go to the right subject matter expert. Reviewers edit, approve or reject each one.
5. **Export.** The tool writes approved answers back into the buyer's original format, and approved edits feed the library for next time.

A tool can only cite what it can find, so keep source content clean and current.

## Benefits of AI RFP software

- **Faster first drafts.** Repeat questions get a sourced draft quickly, so writers start from an answer.
- **Less load on experts.** Subject matter experts review edge cases and skip questions the library already answers.
- **More consistent answers.** Every response draws on the same approved content.
- **Easier verification.** Citations let reviewers check each claim against its source.
- **Room for more bids.** Teams can take on more RFPs and questionnaires with the same people.

## AI RFP software vs traditional RFP software

| Area | Traditional RFP software | AI RFP tools |
|---|---|---|
| Finding answers | Keyword search over a static Q&A library | Semantic search across the library and live documents |
| First draft | A person copies and adapts saved answers | The tool drafts each answer with sources attached |
| Content upkeep | Owners review library entries on a schedule | Some tools flag conflicting or outdated answers automatically |
| Review | Manual assignment of questions | Routing by confidence, topic or owner |
| Formats | Import and export steps for each file | Direct work in Word, Excel, PDF and portals on many tools |
| Main risk | Stale answers | Confident answers built on stale or wrong sources |

![Table comparing traditional RFP software with AI RFP tools across six areas](/media/d350ce23-a0ff-4ffb-ae90-bbd4f9dc7fc9.webp "1600x1140")

Many established tools, including Loopio and Responsive, have added AI drafting on top of their library model. Newer tools such as Inventive AI, AutoRFP.ai and Arphie center their product pages on retrieval and cited drafting.

## Quick picks by buyer type

- **Best overall:** AutoRFP.ai, with published plans, unlimited users and cited answers across Excel, Word, PDF and portals.
- **Best for large, multi-team response operations:** Responsive, with three editions built around enterprise governance.
- **Best for RFPs plus security questionnaires with cited answers:** Inventive AI, with live sync from SharePoint, Google Drive and Notion and automatic flags for outdated answers.
- **Best for structured, library-led proposal teams:** Loopio, with unlimited projects and multi-step reviews on its Enhanced plan.
- **Best for visible confidence on every answer:** Arphie, which shows source material and a confidence level beside each draft.
- **Best for sales teams that want RFP help inside Slack and Excel:** SiftHub.
- **Best for security questionnaires and trust centers:** Conveyor.

## How we compared these tools

We built this shortlist from the tools Google AI Overviews named in our sampled US searches for "AI RFP software" and three related queries in October 2026. AI answers change often, so treat that sample as directional. We then read each vendor's product pages, pricing page and public documentation in October 2026.

We checked each tool against six questions we could answer from public sources:

1. Does the vendor publish plan tiers, with at least one price, and how do they scale (seats, projects or usage)?
2. Does every AI answer show its source?
3. Does it cover RFPs and security questionnaires in one workflow?
4. Does it sync live knowledge sources such as SharePoint, Google Drive, Notion or Confluence?
5. Does it check answers against requirements or flag stale content before submission?
6. How much admin work does the content library need?

We ranked in that order of priority. Pricing comes first because a team cannot shortlist a tool it cannot budget. AutoRFP.ai and Responsive publish plan tiers with at least one price, so they lead. Responsive ranks above Inventive AI on that criterion even though Inventive AI meets more of questions 2 to 5. Inventive AI publishes a starting price but no tiers, and it meets questions 2 to 5 in full, which puts it ahead of Loopio, whose plans list no price and whose answers come from its library. Arphie, SiftHub and Conveyor publish no prices and are ordered by answer sourcing and scope.

We did not run paid pilots of every tool. Treat this guide as a shortlist, then test your top two on a real questionnaire using our [14-day pilot method](/guides/evaluating-ai-rfp-software).

## How do the 7 tools compare?

| Tool | Best for | Scope | Source on each answer | Knowledge sync | Pricing basis (checked 22 Oct 2026) | Main weakness |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| AutoRFP.ai | Teams that want a listed price | RFPs, DDQs, RFIs, security questionnaires | Yes, with a trust layer | 18+ integrations | From $899 per month, paid yearly | Plans cap projects per year |
| Responsive | Large multi-team response operations | RFPs, security questionnaires, buyer questions | Completeness score (TRACE), sourcing not stated | Premium connectors on Enterprise | Emerging Edition from $10,000 (billing period not stated), higher editions quote only | Advanced AI and reporting sit in the top edition |
| Inventive AI | RFPs plus security questionnaires from scattered knowledge | RFPs, RFIs, security questionnaires, DDQs | Yes | SharePoint, Google Drive, Notion, Confluence, Slack, Salesforce | Usage-based, unlimited users, from $10K per year, quote only | No public tiers, $10K per year floor |
| Loopio | Structured, library-led proposal teams | RFIs, RFPs, security questionnaires, DDQs | Library-based | Salesforce and others as add-ons | Quote only, Foundations includes 10 seats | Multi-step reviews start at the Enhanced plan |
| Arphie | Teams that want confidence levels on every draft | RFPs and questionnaires | Yes, plus a confidence level | Google Drive, SharePoint, Confluence, Notion, Box, Dropbox, Seismic, Highspot, Vanta | Not public | No public pricing, no Microsoft Teams integration listed |
| SiftHub | Sales teams working in Slack, Excel and Word | RFPs, RFIs, security questionnaires, sales questions | Yes | Slack and Teams bots, Excel and Word add-in | Quote only | Pricing is quote only |
| Conveyor | Security questionnaires and trust centers | Security questionnaires, RFPs, trust center | Yes | Confluence, Notion, Slack, LLMs | Free trust center tier, Enterprise custom | Free tier excludes questionnaire automation |

Pricing and features last checked 22 October 2026.

![Table part one: seven AI RFP tools by best fit, scope and answer sourcing](/media/af5ab19c-1f26-4bb8-9ac2-91992a8f0403.webp "1600x1400")

![Table part two: seven AI RFP tools by knowledge sync, pricing basis and main weakness](/media/14dc09b5-cbce-4f41-a30d-e7b24ff43e9a.webp "1600x1400")

## 1. AutoRFP.ai: best overall, with the clearest published pricing

AutoRFP.ai ranks first because it pairs the clearest published pricing of the seven with cited answers. Its Scale plan costs $899 per month paid yearly, and every plan includes unlimited users and all features.

**What stands out:**

- Support for RFPs in Excel, Word, PDF and web portals.
- Response generation with citations and a trust layer, plus content ownership and review schedules.
- Collaboration through Slack, Microsoft Teams and built-in project management.
- ISO 27001:2022 and SOC 2 listed on the pricing page, with a 30-day money-back offer.

**Weakness:** plans are capped by projects per year. Scale covers 24 projects and Accelerate ($1,299 per month paid yearly) covers 50, so a team with rising volume will move up tiers.

**Best for:** small and mid-size teams that want to budget from a public price and add every reviewer at no extra cost.

See the [AutoRFP.ai profile](/tools/autorfp-ai).

## 2. Responsive: best for large enterprise response teams

Responsive suits large organizations that run complex, multi-team response operations. It offers three editions (Emerging, Growth and Enterprise) and AI agents across the pursuit lifecycle.

**What stands out:**

- Coverage of RFPs, security questionnaires and buyer questions.
- TRACE Score, which shows whether an answer covers every part of a question (quoted by a Tenable proposal manager on Responsive's site).
- Unlimited response projects and unlimited content and collaboration from the Emerging Edition up.
- Enterprise options for security controls, flexible hosting and premium connectors.

**Weakness:** the deepest features sit in the top tier. Flexible custom AI, advanced reporting and premium connectors are listed under Enterprise Edition, and only the Emerging Edition shows a starting price: $10,000 (billing period not stated).

**Best for:** enterprises with a central proposal team and many contributors who need governance and control.

See the [Responsive profile](/tools/responsive).

## 3. Inventive AI: best for RFPs plus security questionnaires with cited answers

Inventive AI is the strongest pick for teams that answer RFPs and security questionnaires from knowledge spread across many tools. It meets all four of our sourcing, scope, knowledge sync and stale content questions, and ranks third only because it publishes a starting price without tiers. Every AI-generated answer includes source citations from your documents and past responses, so reviewers can check each claim quickly.

**What stands out:**

- A unified knowledge hub that syncs content from SharePoint, Google Drive and Notion, with integrations for Confluence, Slack and Salesforce.
- An AI Content Manager that scans connected sources and flags conflicting or outdated answers. This targets stale answers, the main risk of AI drafting.
- AI agents for go/no-go decisions, competitive intelligence and win themes, plus requirements and compliance agents that check responses before submission.
- Coverage of RFPs, RFIs, security questionnaires and DDQs in one product.
- Usage-based pricing with unlimited users, so subject matter experts can join without seat costs.

**Weakness:** Inventive AI publishes no price tiers. Its pricing page lists a fixed platform fee plus usage, says plans start at $10K per year, and asks for a 15-minute call to get a quote. We found no self-serve trial on its site (22 October 2026). Teams with a handful of RFPs a year may find that floor high.

**Best for:** presales, solutions and proposal teams that handle both RFPs and security reviews and keep their knowledge in several systems.

See the [Inventive AI profile](/tools/inventive-ai) or the [Inventive AI vs Loopio comparison](/compare/inventive-ai-vs-loopio).

## 4. Loopio: best for library-led proposal teams

Loopio is best for proposal teams that run on a structured, governed answer library. Every plan includes unlimited projects, unlimited library entries and generative AI.

**What stands out:**

- Four permission levels per project (No Access, Participant, Creator, Full Access).
- Multi-step reviews, confidential projects and a multi-language library on the Enhanced plan.
- Separate business units and sandboxes on Enterprise.
- Coverage of RFIs, RFPs, security questionnaires, DDQs and sales proposals.

**Weakness:** multi-step reviews only start at the Enhanced plan, and project translations and industry integrations such as Salesforce are add-ons. The entry Foundations plan includes 10 seats, and all pricing is by quote.

**Best for:** established proposal teams that value library structure and review gates.

See the [Loopio profile](/tools/loopio) or [Loopio alternatives](/alternatives/loopio).

## 5. Arphie: confidence levels on every answer

Arphie shows the source material and a confidence level beside each drafted answer. Its own guide explains how confidence bands should map to answer acceptance, which helps teams decide what to review first.

**What stands out:**

- Answers that expose source material and confidence levels, in Arphie's own description of its product.
- Published guidance on calibrating confidence bands, so a high-confidence answer should need fewer edits than a low-confidence one.
- Integrations with Google Drive, SharePoint, Confluence, Notion, Box, Dropbox, Highspot, Seismic and Vanta, plus an MCP connector for tools like Claude and ChatGPT.

**Weakness:** Arphie publishes no pricing. Its pricing page was not publicly viewable when we checked on 22 October 2026, so budgeting needs a sales call. Its integrations page lists Slack for notifications and quick questions but no Microsoft Teams integration, so Teams-first companies should ask about the roadmap.

**Best for:** teams that want reviewers to see evidence quality on every answer.

## 6. SiftHub: best for sales teams in Slack and Excel

SiftHub works best for sales and presales teams that want RFP help inside the tools they already use. It offers an RFP Agent on its own or as part of a broader sales platform.

**What stands out:**

- An Excel and Word add-in for working directly in buyer files.
- Bots for Slack and Microsoft Teams that answer questions and follow-ups.
- Drafts grounded in verified content with sources attached.
- SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001:2022 certification listed on its site.

**Weakness:** pricing is quote only, and SiftHub sells a broader sales-agent platform (battlecards, search and more), so teams that only need RFP response should scope the RFP Agent package alone.

**Best for:** sales-led teams that want RFP, security and sales questions answered in Slack and Excel.

See the [SiftHub profile](/tools/sifthub).

## 7. Conveyor: best for security questionnaires

Conveyor is best for teams whose main load is security questionnaires and customer trust reviews. Its platform combines security questionnaire automation, a trust center and an RFP response product.

**What stands out:**

- AI that reads and maps every question and field in Word and spreadsheet files.
- Q&A upkeep from Slack (emoji reactions) and from LLMs such as Claude or ChatGPT.
- A free trust center tier for sharing security documents.

**Weakness:** the free tier excludes questionnaire automation and integrations, and the Enterprise plan is custom priced. Teams with heavy narrative RFPs should test long-form answers closely.

**Best for:** security, compliance and presales teams that field many security reviews.

## Can these tools submit answers without human review?

No tool on this list should send answers without a person signing off. AI drafts can sound confident while relying on an outdated policy, a retired product feature or a source that does not answer the full question. Keep a named owner for security, legal and pricing answers, and require review of every low-confidence draft. Good tools make review faster, and a person still signs off. Answer quality also depends on the content library: retire outdated answers, name an owner for each topic and review high-traffic answers on a set schedule.

## How much does AI RFP software cost?

Prices below were checked on vendor sites on 22 October 2026. Confirm them before you buy.

| Tool | Published price | Model | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| AutoRFP.ai | Scale $899 per month and Accelerate $1,299 per month, paid yearly | Projects per year, unlimited users | [autorfp.ai pricing](https://autorfp.ai/pricing) |
| Responsive | Emerging Edition from $10,000 (billing period not stated) | Editions, contact sales | [responsive.io pricing](https://www.responsive.io/pricing) |
| Inventive AI | Plans start at $10K per year | Usage-based, unlimited users, custom quote | [inventive.ai pricing](https://www.inventive.ai/inventive-ai-pricing) |
| Loopio | Not published | Quote, Foundations includes 10 seats | [loopio.com pricing](https://loopio.com/pricing/) |
| Arphie | Not published | Contact sales | [arphie.ai](https://www.arphie.ai/) |
| SiftHub | Not published | Quote, RFP Agent or full platform | [sifthub.io pricing](https://www.sifthub.io/pricing) |
| Conveyor | Free trust center tier, Enterprise custom | Credits and custom plans | [conveyor.com pricing](https://www.conveyor.com/pricing) |

For a lower-cost reference point outside our seven, RFP.ai lists a Starter plan at €49 per month (€40.83 per month billed annually) and one-time credit packs from €39 on [its pricing page](https://rfp.ai/pricing).

Three pricing models dominate: per seat, per project and usage-based. If many subject matter experts review answers, unlimited-user plans (Inventive AI, AutoRFP.ai) usually cost less to roll out.

## How to choose an RFP response tool

1. **Count your volume.** List RFPs and security questionnaires per year. Project caps and usage pricing look very different at 20 versus 200.
2. **Map your knowledge.** Note where approved answers live today. Pick a tool that syncs those sources directly.
3. **Check citations.** Every answer should show its source. Reject tools that hide it.
4. **Test stale content.** Plant one outdated answer in the pilot and see whether the tool flags it.
5. **Test your hardest format.** Use your messiest Excel questionnaire or portal.
6. **Price the full team.** Include every reviewer, translation and integration add-on.
7. **Run a two-week pilot.** Use the same questionnaire and sources in each tool. Our [full evaluation checklist](/guides/evaluating-ai-rfp-software) covers each step.

Browse every tool in our [RFP and proposal software category](/categories/rfp-software), or compare [Inventive AI alternatives](/alternatives/inventive-ai).

## FAQ

### What is AI RFP software?
AI RFP software reads an incoming RFP, RFI, DDQ or security questionnaire, finds approved answers in your company knowledge, drafts a cited response for each question, and routes uncertain items to a human reviewer before export.

### What is the best AI RFP tool in 2026?
AutoRFP.ai is the best AI RFP software overall in our ranking because we rank published pricing first, and it pairs public plan prices with unlimited users and cited answers. Responsive suits large enterprise teams, and Inventive AI is the strongest pick for RFPs plus security questionnaires with cited answers.

### What is the difference between AI RFP software and AI RFP response software?
They describe the same category. Both terms mean software that drafts answers to RFPs and questionnaires from your approved knowledge, with human review before submission.

### How much does AI RFP software cost?
On 22 October 2026, AutoRFP.ai listed plans from $899 per month paid yearly, Inventive AI listed plans from $10K per year, and Responsive listed its Emerging Edition from $10,000 (billing period not stated). Loopio, Arphie and SiftHub price by quote.

### Can AI RFP tools answer security questionnaires?
Yes. All seven tools on this list support security questionnaires, and Conveyor specializes in them.

### Does AI RFP software replace proposal writers?
No. AI RFP software drafts first answers and handles repeat questions, while people still own strategy, win themes, sensitive answers and final sign-off.

### How long does setup take?
Setup time depends mostly on how clean and connected your source content is. Tools that sync existing systems such as SharePoint or Google Drive avoid a full library rebuild, but every tool needs review of its first answers.

| Replit | Platform | Browser app building | Core $20/mo ($18/mo yearly) | No standalone free plan listed | $20 toward stronger models on Core |

Prices are in USD before tax, from each vendor's pricing page on 22 Oct 2026.

![Table of type, entry paid price and free option for ten Cursor alternatives](/media/8760771b-1f4c-4a22-8f98-98334b3ebc32.webp "1600x1420")

## Why are developers leaving Cursor in 2026?

Cost and model access are the main reasons. Cursor's Plus plan includes Grok models only, and its FAQ says Premium and above do not include an allowance for third-party models, so Claude and GPT in Cursor are paid at API list price ([Cursor pricing](https://cursor.com/pricing)).

Usage now comes from one pool shared across Cursor and Grok, with a weekly refresh.

| Cursor plan | Price | What you get |
|---|---|---|
| Free | $0 | Limited agent and chat requests |
| Plus | $8/mo | Shared usage pool, Grok models only |
| Premium | $30/mo | 4x Plus usage, third-party models at API list price |
| Super | $100/mo | 15x Plus usage, priority access at peak times |
| Ultra | $200/mo | 50x Plus usage, earliest access to models |
| Teams | $30+/user/mo | Pooled usage |

## 1. GitHub Copilot: which Cursor alternative is cheapest?

[GitHub Copilot](https://trutool.co/tools/github-copilot) has the lowest entry paid plan of the subscription picks, at $10 a month for Pro. Its free plan includes limited chat and agent usage and supports the CLI and agent mode ([GitHub Copilot plans](https://github.com/features/copilot/plans)).

If your work lives on GitHub, Copilot is the most direct switch, since code review, Copilot in the cloud and the Copilot app run inside GitHub. It also works in VS Code.

**Strengths**

- Pro+ is $39 and Max is $100 a month, with total GitHub AI Credits of $15, $70 and $200 across Pro, Pro+ and Max.
- Copilot Business costs $19 per seat a month and Enterprise $39 per seat a month ([GitHub Docs](https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/get-started/plans)).

**Weakness**

- Part of each plan's credits is a "flex allotment" that GitHub says may change over time, so monthly capacity is less predictable than the sticker price.

**Best for:** developers who work on GitHub.

## 2. Claude Code: which Cursor alternative is best for agent work on Claude?

[Claude Code](https://trutool.co/tools/claude-code) is the strongest choice if Claude models were your main reason for using Cursor. It comes with Claude Pro and Max, so you pay a flat subscription and skip API metering ([Claude pricing](https://claude.com/pricing)).

**Strengths**

- Max starts at $100 a month with a choice of 5x or 20x Pro usage.
- Team premium seats with Claude Code cost $100 per seat a month billed yearly, or $125 monthly.

**Weakness**

- Claude Code is not on the free plan, and every plan has usage limits. Max starts at five times the Pro price.

**Best for:** terminal agents on Claude at a flat monthly price.

## 3. OpenAI Codex: which Cursor alternative suits ChatGPT subscribers?

[OpenAI Codex](https://trutool.co/tools/openai-codex) is the easiest switch if you already pay for ChatGPT. Codex is included in ChatGPT Free, Go, Plus, Pro, Business, Edu and Enterprise plans ([Codex pricing](https://developers.openai.com/codex/pricing)).

**Strengths**

- Plus at $20 a month adds Codex on the web, CLI, IDE extension and iOS, plus automatic code review and Slack.
- Pro plans cost $100, $200 or $500 a month, and Business is $20 per user billed yearly ($25 monthly).
- An API key option bills at API prices, which suits CI jobs.

**Weakness**

- Free and Go ($8) are limited to GPT-6 Luna in the desktop app, subject to rollout, so the full set of Codex surfaces starts at Plus.

**Best for:** ChatGPT Plus or Pro subscribers.

## 4. Devin Desktop (formerly Windsurf): which Cursor alternative is closest to Cursor?

[Devin Desktop](https://trutool.co/tools/devin) is the closest like-for-like editor swap. Windsurf.com now redirects to Devin Desktop, and Pro includes frontier models in the plan ([Devin pricing](https://devin.ai/pricing)).

**Strengths**

- The free plan has a light agent quota plus unlimited inline edits and Tab completions.
- Pro at $20 includes models from OpenAI, Claude, Gemini and SpaceXAI, free use of SWE-2 and Devin Cloud agents.
- Teams costs $80 a month plus $40 per full dev seat, for up to 200 users.

**Weakness**

- Quotas are described only as "increased" or "significantly higher", with no published numbers, so heavy users should test limits first.

**Best for:** Cursor users who want the same editor workflow with major models in the plan.

## 5. Zed: which Cursor alternative is the fastest editor?

[Zed](https://trutool.co/tools/zed) is an open source code editor that stays free with your own API keys or external agents such as Claude Agent and Codex CLI ([Zed pricing](https://zed.dev/pricing), [Zed FAQ](https://zed.dev/faq)).

**Strengths**

- Pro at $10 a month adds unlimited edit predictions and $5 of tokens, with a 14-day trial that needs no card.
- Business costs $30 per seat a month.

**Weakness**

- Pro includes only $5 of tokens, and further usage is billed at API list price plus 10%.

**Best for:** developers who want a fast native editor and their own models.

## 6. Cline: which Cursor alternative is a free agent inside VS Code?

[Cline](https://trutool.co/tools/cline) is a free, open source coding agent that works in VS Code and the command line. Individuals pay only for AI inference ([Cline pricing](https://cline.bot/pricing)).

**Strengths**

- No subscriptions or seat fees for the open source version.
- Bring keys from Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, OpenRouter, AWS Bedrock, DeepSeek and more, or buy inference at cost.

**Weakness**

- The JetBrains extension, SSO and team management are Enterprise features, and total cost depends on how many tokens you use.

**Best for:** VS Code users who want control over models and costs.

## 7. OpenCode: which Cursor alternative works with subscriptions you already have?

[OpenCode](https://trutool.co/tools/opencode) is a free, MIT-licensed coding agent for the terminal, desktop and IDE. It can sign in with Claude Pro or Max, ChatGPT Plus or Pro, or GitHub Copilot ([OpenCode](https://opencode.ai/)).

**Strengths**

- Ships with free models that need no account.
- Connects to 75+ LLM providers, including local models.

**Weakness**

- OpenCode says it stores your data when you use its free models, so privacy-sensitive teams should connect their own provider.

**Best for:** developers who already pay for Claude, ChatGPT or Copilot.

## 8. Kiro: which Cursor alternative has the clearest credit pricing?

[Kiro](https://trutool.co/tools/kiro) publishes exact credit counts for every plan, which makes costs easy to forecast ([Kiro pricing](https://kiro.dev/pricing/)).

**Strengths**

- Free tier with 50 credits, including Claude Sonnet 4.5 and open-weight models, with limits.
- Pro $20 (1,000 credits), Pro+ $40 (2,000), Pro Max $100 (5,000) and Power $200 (10,000) a month.
- Paid plans include Claude Sonnet 5 and Claude Opus 5, and add-on credits cost $0.04 each.

**Weakness**

- Credits burn at different rates by model. Kiro's pricing page says a task run with Sonnet 4.6 costs 1.3x the credits of the same task in Auto.

**Best for:** teams that want predictable, metered pricing.

## 9. JetBrains AI: which Cursor alternative fits JetBrains IDE users?

[JetBrains AI](https://trutool.co/tools/jetbrains) adds AI features inside JetBrains IDEs, priced in AI credits worth $1 each ([JetBrains AI licensing](https://www.jetbrains.com/help/ai-assistant/licensing-and-subscriptions.html)).

**Strengths**

- AI Free includes 3 credits per 30 days.
- For individuals, AI Pro is $10/mo with 10 credits and AI Ultimate is $30/mo with 35 credits.

**Weakness**

- Organization licenses cost $20 for AI Pro and $60 for AI Ultimate per user, and 10 credits per 30 days on individual AI Pro may not cover heavy agent work.

**Best for:** teams standardized on JetBrains IDEs.

## 10. Replit: which Cursor alternative is best for building apps in the browser?

[Replit](https://trutool.co/tools/replit) suits people who want to build, run and host an app from the browser with an AI agent ([Replit pricing](https://replit.com/pricing)).

**Strengths**

- Core at $20 a month ($18 yearly) includes up to 30 hours of chat and 60 projects in Free Mode, plus $20 toward stronger models.
- Pro at $100 a month ($90 yearly) adds 10 parallel agents and up to 15 collaborators.

**Weakness**

- Replit is a hosted platform, so it fits an existing local codebase less well than an editor or terminal agent.

**Best for:** founders building web apps end to end.

## What are the best free Cursor alternatives?

The best free Cursor alternatives are Cline, OpenCode and Zed, which cost nothing beyond the models you connect. These are the strongest free picks if you want to avoid a subscription:

- **OpenCode** includes free models, so you can start without an API key.
- **Cline** is free for individuals. You pay only for inference or use your own keys.
- **Zed** is free forever with your own keys or external agents.
- **GitHub Copilot Free** gives limited chat and agent usage, and **Kiro Free** gives 50 credits.

## Which open source Cursor alternatives are worth using?

Cline, OpenCode and Zed are the open source alternatives to the Cursor AI code editor worth shortlisting. OpenCode is MIT licensed and runs in the terminal, desktop and IDEs. Cline's open source extension runs in VS Code and the CLI. Zed is an open source editor that works with your own keys and with agents such as Claude Agent and Codex CLI.

Start with the models you want. If you mostly used Claude in Cursor, Claude Code or a Claude key in Cline gives you a flat or at-cost price. If you mostly used GPT, Codex with ChatGPT Plus is the simplest route.

Next, decide between an editor and an agent. Devin Desktop, Zed and JetBrains AI keep an editor-first workflow, while Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode and Cline are agent-first. These tools also count usage differently: Copilot, Kiro and JetBrains use credits, Claude and Codex use plan limits, and Cline, OpenCode and Zed with your own keys pass API costs through.

Finally, run a one-week trial on a real repository and compare actual spend before you cancel Cursor. For a structured trial, see [how to choose an AI coding tool](https://trutool.co/guides/choosing-ai-coding-tools). TruTool also lists more alternatives to Cursor in its [Cursor alternatives directory](https://trutool.co/alternatives/cursor).

## FAQ

### What are the best free alternatives to Cursor AI?

The best free alternatives to Cursor AI are Cline, OpenCode and Zed. OpenCode includes free models, while Cline and Zed are free when you bring your own API keys. GitHub Copilot and Kiro also offer limited free plans.

### What is the cheapest Cursor alternative?

The cheapest paid option is ChatGPT Go at $8 a month, which includes Codex but only GPT-6 Luna in the desktop app. For a full coding plan, GitHub Copilot Pro, Zed Pro and JetBrains AI Pro each cost $10 a month. Cursor's own cheapest paid plan, Plus at $8, includes Grok models only.

### What are some Cursor alternatives for teams?

GitHub Copilot Business costs $19 per seat a month, Codex Business is $20 per user a month billed yearly, and Zed Business is $30 per seat a month. Devin Teams costs $80 a month plus $40 per full seat, and Claude Team premium seats with Claude Code are $100 per seat a month billed yearly.

### Which Cursor alternative includes Claude models in the price?

Claude Code includes Claude models in Claude Pro ($20 a month) and Max (from $100 a month). Devin Desktop Pro at $20 a month and Kiro Pro at $20 a month also include Claude models.

### Why are people looking for Cursor alternatives?

Cursor is now sold directly through X Subscription Corp., and its Plus plan includes Grok models only. On Premium and above, Claude and GPT usage is billed separately at API list price, which raises costs for developers who relied on those models.

**Quick answer:** The best AI tools for marketing in 2026 are ChatGPT and Claude for drafting, Jasper for brand content, Semrush and Surfer for SEO, Canva for design, Descript and OpusClip for video, Buffer for social, HubSpot for automation and Zapier for connecting apps. Nine of the 12 have a full free plan.

Picking AI tools for marketing starts with one bottleneck and one tool that fixes it. We checked the official pricing page of every tool below on October 23, 2026. Prices change often, so confirm before you buy.

## Key facts at a glance

- ChatGPT Plus costs $20/month, billed monthly only, per OpenAI's help center.
- Claude Pro costs $17/month on annual billing or $20 monthly.
- Jasper has no free plan. Pro is $59/seat/month yearly or $69 monthly.
- Semrush's SEO plan is $139/month, or $117.33/month billed annually.
- Buffer starts at $5 per channel per month on Essentials.
- Canva Pro is from $144 a year, and HubSpot Marketing Hub Starter lists at $20 per seat per month.
- Nine tools offer a full free plan: ChatGPT, Claude, Canva, Grammarly, Descript, OpusClip, Buffer, HubSpot and Zapier. Semrush adds a limited free AI Visibility tier.

## What are the best AI tools for marketing in 2026?

The best AI tools for marketing in 2026 are ChatGPT, Claude, Jasper, Canva, Semrush, Surfer, Grammarly, Descript, OpusClip, Buffer, HubSpot and Zapier. Each one wins a different marketing job. Most teams need three or four of them, one per bottleneck.

The table below compares them on price, free access and fit.

![Comparison table of 12 AI tools for marketing with best use, free plan and starting price](/media/7502e6a0-8d29-4fd1-a5bb-08e4bfc9b6c5.webp)

| Tool | Best for | Free plan | Starting paid price (official page, Oct 23, 2026) | Main weakness |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ChatGPT | Drafting, research, images | Yes | Plus $20/mo (monthly only) | No annual billing for Plus |
| Claude | Long-form writing, analysis | Yes | Pro $17/mo annual, $20 monthly | Heavy users get pushed to Max, from $100/mo |
| Jasper | On-brand content for teams | No (free trial) | Pro $59/seat/mo yearly, $69 monthly | Priced per seat, costly for big teams |
| Canva | Social and ad design | Yes | Pro from $144/year | Trial AI allowance equals the free plan |
| Semrush | SEO and AI search visibility | No full plan (limited free AI Visibility tier) | SEO $139/mo, $117.33/mo annual | Expensive for solo marketers |
| Surfer | Content optimization | No | Discovery $49/mo billed yearly | AI visibility tracking starts at a higher tier |
| Grammarly | Editing and tone | Yes | Pro $12/mo billed annually ($144/yr) | Best price needs an annual commitment |
| Descript | Video and podcast editing | Yes | Hobbyist $16/mo annual, $24 monthly | Media hours and AI credits are capped per plan |
| OpusClip | Short clips from long video | Yes (60 credits/mo) | Starter $15/mo | Credit-based, long videos burn credits fast |
| Buffer | Social scheduling | Yes | Essentials $5/channel/mo | Cost scales with every channel you add |
| HubSpot | CRM-led marketing automation | Yes (up to 2 users) | Marketing Hub Starter from $20/seat/mo list | Professional jumps to $890/mo |
| Zapier | Connecting your stack | Yes | Professional from $19.99/mo | Complex Zaps get pricey on higher plans |

## How did we choose these AI marketing tools?

We chose tools that cover one clear marketing job, publish pricing on an official page, and are named in current top-ranking roundups from HubSpot, Zapier and Search Engine Land. We left out tools that hide pricing entirely, because buyers cannot compare them. This list also leaves out ad-platform features such as Google Ads Smart Bidding and Meta Advantage+, and email-first platforms like Klaviyo, which suit a separate guide.

Each tool below lists one weakness, drawn from its pricing page and plan limits.

Browse every tool we list in [marketing tools](/categories/marketing).

## Which AI tools are best for writing marketing content?

ChatGPT, Claude, Jasper and Grammarly are the strongest AI writing tools for marketers. ChatGPT and Claude are general assistants that draft, research and rework copy. Jasper adds brand controls for teams. Grammarly sits on top of all of them as an editor.

### 1. ChatGPT

**Best for:** Drafting, research and images

ChatGPT is the most flexible starting point. The free plan includes unlimited text chats, limited image creation and limited deep research, per OpenAI's pricing page.

Plus costs $20/month and adds expanded deep research, projects, scheduled tasks and custom GPTs. That makes it useful for recurring jobs like weekly content briefs.

**Weakness:** Plus has no annual billing option, so there is no discount for committing. The Go plan may also include ads.

Read our [ChatGPT review](/tools/chatgpt) or compare it in [Claude vs ChatGPT](/guides/claude-vs-chatgpt).

### 2. Claude

**Best for:** Long-form writing and analysis

Claude suits long-form writing and analysis, such as turning research notes into a whitepaper draft. There is a free plan.

Claude Pro is $17/month on annual billing or $20 monthly. Team standard seats are $20/seat/month annually or $25 monthly.

**Weakness:** marketers who work in it all day can hit limits, and Max starts at $100/month.

See our [Claude review](/tools/claude).

### 3. Jasper

**Best for:** On-brand content for teams

Jasper is built for marketing teams that need many writers to sound like one brand. It positions itself on brand consistency at scale.

Pro is $59/seat/month billed yearly or $69 monthly. A free trial is available.

**Weakness:** there is no free plan, and per-seat pricing adds up quickly for larger teams.

More in our [Jasper review](/tools/jasper).

### 4. Grammarly

**Best for:** Editing and tone

Grammarly checks grammar, clarity and tone across email, docs and social posts. The free plan covers spelling and grammar.

Pro is $12/month billed annually, which is $144 a year.

**Weakness:** the advertised price assumes annual billing, and the tool only works on copy you have already written.

See the [Grammarly review](/tools/grammarly).

## Which AI tools help with SEO and AI search?

Semrush and Surfer are the two picks here. Semrush covers keyword research, competitor data and AI visibility tracking in one suite. Surfer focuses on optimizing individual pages so they cover a topic fully. Pick Semrush for research breadth and Surfer for on-page work.

### 5. Semrush

**Best for:** SEO and AI search visibility

Semrush is an SEO suite for keyword research, competitor analysis and tracking brand visibility in AI search. Its SEO plan costs $139/month, or $117.33/month billed annually. Its pricing page also lists a free AI Visibility tier for trying the platform.

**Weakness:** the entry price is high for freelancers, and extra users start at $45/month each.

Read our [Semrush review](/tools/semrush).

### 6. Surfer

**Best for:** Content optimization

Surfer's Discovery plan is $49/month billed yearly and covers drafting and optimizing content. AI search analytics across ChatGPT and other engines appear on higher plans, from $82/month billed yearly.

**Weakness:** no free plan, and the AI visibility features sit above the entry tier.

See our [Surfer review](/tools/surfer).

## Which AI tools are best for marketing design and video?

Canva is the default for design. Descript and OpusClip split video: Descript edits long recordings like webinars and podcasts by editing the transcript, and OpusClip cuts long videos into short social clips. All three have a free plan, so you can test before paying.

### 7. Canva

**Best for:** Social and ad design

Canva is free for individuals. Canva Pro starts from $144 a year for one person in the US, before tax, and adds Brand Kits, Magic Resize, Magic Write, background removal and AI ad creation with Canva Grow, per Canva's Pro page.

**Weakness:** Canva says the AI allowance during a Pro trial is the same as Canva Free, so you cannot fully test AI limits before paying. Pro is also limited to one person.

See our [Canva review](/tools/canva) and [Figma vs Canva](/compare/figma-vs-canva).

### 8. Descript

**Best for:** Video and podcast editing

Descript lets you edit video by editing text. The free plan is a starting point. Hobbyist is $16/month billed annually or $24 monthly, with 10 media hours and 400 AI credits a month.

**Weakness:** media hours and AI credits are capped on every plan, which heavy video teams will feel.

More in the [Descript review](/tools/descript).

### 9. OpusClip

**Best for:** Short clips from long video

OpusClip turns long videos into short clips. The free plan gives 60 credits per month. Starter is $15/month with 150 credits, and Pro is $29/month.

**Weakness:** everything runs on credits, so long source videos use your allowance fast.

See the [OpusClip review](/tools/opusclip).

## Which AI tools handle social media and automation?

Buffer, HubSpot and Zapier cover distribution and automation. Buffer schedules social posts cheaply, HubSpot runs email and CRM-driven campaigns, and Zapier connects every other tool on this list so content moves between them without copy and paste.

### 10. Buffer

**Best for:** Social scheduling

Buffer's free plan connects up to 3 channels with 10 scheduled posts per channel. Essentials is $5/month per channel and Team is $10/month per channel, billed yearly.

**Weakness:** pricing is per channel, so a brand on six networks pays six times the base rate.

See our [Buffer review](/tools/buffer) or the [Hootsuite review](/tools/hootsuite).

### 11. HubSpot

**Best for:** CRM-led marketing automation

HubSpot Marketing Hub combines CRM, email and automation with AI agents. The free plan covers up to 2 users. Marketing Hub Starter lists at $20/month per Core Seat with 1,000 marketing contacts and 500 HubSpot Credits a month, per HubSpot's product catalog.

**Weakness:** the jump from Starter to Professional is steep, as Professional starts at $890/month. Extra AI usage is billed in credits, which makes costs harder to predict.

Read the [HubSpot review](/tools/hubspot) and our [marketing platform checklist](/guides/choosing-marketing-platforms).

### 12. Zapier

**Best for:** Connecting your stack

Zapier connects your marketing apps. The free plan includes Zaps, Tables and Forms with 100 tasks per month. Professional starts at $19.99/month and Team at $69/month.

**Weakness:** costs rise as automations get more complex, and AI agents and chatbots are priced as separate add-ons.

See the [Zapier review](/tools/zapier).

## How do you choose the right AI tool for marketing?

Choose the right AI tool for marketing by naming the one task that slows your team most, then picking the cheapest tool that fixes it. Test it on the free plan or trial for real work, check how pricing scales with seats, channels or credits, and only then commit annually.

A simple order works for most small teams:

1. Start with one general assistant (ChatGPT or Claude).
2. Add one channel tool where you publish most (Canva, Buffer or Descript).
3. Add SEO tooling once content volume justifies it.
4. Connect everything with Zapier last.

For a deeper buying checklist, see [How to choose marketing platforms](/guides/choosing-marketing-platforms).

## Frequently asked questions

### What are the best AI tools for marketing?
The best AI tools for marketing in 2026 include ChatGPT and Claude for writing, Jasper for brand content, Semrush and Surfer for SEO, Canva for design, Descript and OpusClip for video, Buffer for social, HubSpot for automation and Zapier for connecting apps.

### Are there free AI tools for marketing?
Yes. ChatGPT, Claude, Canva, Grammarly, Descript, OpusClip, Buffer, HubSpot and Zapier all have full free plans as of October 2026, and Semrush has a limited free AI Visibility tier. Free tiers have usage limits, so they suit testing and light use.

### Which AI marketing tool is best for small businesses?
For small businesses, ChatGPT or Claude plus Canva covers most needs at low cost. Add Buffer at $5 per channel for scheduling. Move to Semrush or HubSpot once traffic and lead volume justify the higher price.

### Is ChatGPT enough for marketing?
ChatGPT handles drafting, research and images well, but it does not schedule posts, track rankings or run email campaigns. Most teams pair it with a design tool, a social scheduler and an SEO tool.

### How much do AI marketing tools cost?
Entry-level paid plans range from $5 per channel per month (Buffer Essentials) to $139/month (Semrush SEO, billed monthly). Most writing assistants cost around $20/month. Team and pro tiers run higher, for example HubSpot Marketing Hub Professional from $890/month.

![Ten AI presentation makers compared for 2026, with free plans and pricing checked](/media/7641cdcd-b0cf-43b2-b23c-eb90f03d3751.webp)

Looking for the best AI presentation maker in 2026? This guide compares 10 tools that turn a prompt, document or outline into a slide deck. We cover free plans, PowerPoint export, Google Slides support, brand kits and what a team of five really pays, using prices checked on vendor pages on 25 Oct 2026.

Most pages ranking for this topic are written by vendors that rank their own product first. This guide compares all 10 on vendor pricing pages, help docs and public reviews.

## Quick answer: what is the best AI presentation maker in 2026?

The best AI presentation maker in 2026 for most people is Gamma, because it turns a short prompt into a full, styled deck in one step. If you live in PowerPoint or Google Slides, pick Plus AI. Designers should choose Canva, and anyone who needs a solid free tier should start with Presentations.ai.

- Best overall: [Gamma](https://trutool.co/guides/best-ai-presentation-maker#1-gamma-which-ai-presentation-maker-is-best-overall), fast prompt-to-deck with a free starter allowance.
- Best for PowerPoint and Google Slides: [Plus AI](https://trutool.co/guides/best-ai-presentation-maker#2-plus-ai-which-ai-presentation-maker-works-inside-powerpoint-and-google-slides), works inside the apps you already use.
- Best for design and brand kits: [Canva](https://trutool.co/guides/best-ai-presentation-maker#3-canva-which-ai-presentation-maker-is-best-for-design-and-brand-kits).
- Best free plan: [Presentations.ai](https://trutool.co/guides/best-ai-presentation-maker#8-presentations-ai-which-ai-presentation-maker-has-the-best-free-plan), 200 credits and up to 20 slides at $0.

![Quick picks: Gamma, Plus AI, Canva and Presentations.ai for different presentation needs](/media/96a74ac8-e837-4eb0-b820-861f7dad7a43.webp)

## How do the best AI presentation makers compare?

The best AI presentation makers split into two groups. Standalone tools like Gamma, Beautiful.ai, Pitch and Presentations.ai build decks in their own editors. Add-ons like Plus AI, SlidesAI, Copilot and Gemini work inside PowerPoint or Google Slides. The table below shows free plans, starting annual prices and export support side by side.

![Best AI presentation maker comparison table for 2026](/media/39f42368-6169-42f6-a604-f08205315a1f.webp)

| Tool | Best for | Free plan | Starting price (annual) | PowerPoint export | Google Slides | Brand kit |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Gamma | Fast prompt-to-deck | Yes, 400 one-time credits | Check current pricing on the vendor site | Yes (PPTX export) | Export available | Yes, on paid plans |
| Plus AI | Inside PowerPoint and Google Slides | No, free trial | $10/user/mo | Native (add-in) | Native (add-on) | Uses your templates |
| Canva | Design and brand kits | Yes, free for individuals | Check current pricing on the vendor site | Yes (PPTX download) | Export available | Yes, paid plans |
| Beautiful.ai | Brand-consistent business decks | No, 14-day trial (card) | $14.50/mo (Pro) | Yes | Export available | Yes |
| Microsoft Copilot in PowerPoint | Microsoft 365 teams | Copilot Chat only | $18/user/mo add-on (promo to 31 Dec 2026) | Native | No | Uses your templates |
| Gemini in Google Slides | Google Workspace teams | No, 14-day trial | Check current pricing on the vendor site | Via Slides export | Native | Uses your themes |
| Pitch | Team collaboration | Yes, up to 5 members | €15/mo (Plus) | Yes | Import supported | Yes |
| Presentations.ai | Free use | Yes, 200 credits, 20 slides | $20/mo (Pro) | Yes | Check on vendor | Yes, paid plans |
| Prezi | Non-linear, zooming talks | Yes, Basic | Check current pricing on the vendor site | Limited (PDF/video focus) | No | Yes, paid plans |
| SlidesAI | Cheapest Google Slides add-on | Yes, 200 credits/mo | $10/user/mo (Pro) | Via Slides export | Native (add-on) | Limited |

*Prices checked on vendor pages on 25 Oct 2026. Export and brand kit details come from vendor feature pages and public reviews.*

## How did we compare these AI presentation makers?

We compared these AI presentation makers on five things buyers actually hit: how fast they produce a usable first draft, whether the deck exports cleanly to PowerPoint, Google Slides support, brand controls, and real cost. Prices come from official vendor pricing pages checked on 25 Oct 2026. Feature notes come from vendor docs and public reviews.

We did not assign scores. A number without a documented method is noise, so each tool gets a plain "best for" label and one honest weakness instead.

Export matters more than most lists admit. A deck that looks great in a web editor but breaks when your client opens the PPTX is a deck you rebuild by hand.

We also weighted what you already pay for. If your company has Microsoft 365 or Google Workspace, the AI inside those suites may be enough, and we say when a standalone tool is still worth it.

## Why is Tome missing from this list?

Tome is missing because it no longer exists as a presentation tool. Tome shut down its slides product in April 2025 and pivoted to Lightfield, a CRM. Its site now returns a 404. If a "best AI presentation maker" list still ranks Tome as a pick, that list is stale and its other recommendations may be too.

Tome was one of the first AI deck builders to go viral, which is why it still appears in older roundups. Users who did not export their decks before the shutdown lost them.

The lesson for buyers is simple. Pick a tool with a clean export path, so your decks survive if the vendor changes direction.

## 1. Gamma: which AI presentation maker is best overall?

Gamma is the best AI presentation maker overall for turning one prompt into a complete deck. Type a prompt or paste notes and it returns a complete, styled deck, with layouts, images and text already placed. Free users get 400 one-time credits to try it. Paid plan prices were not confirmed, so check current pricing on the vendor site.

**Best for:** founders, marketers and students who want a good-looking first draft fast.

**Pricing:** Free plan with 400 credits that do not refresh, plus 200 bonus credits per referral up to 2,000. Paid plans refill credits monthly (Plus includes 1,000 per month). Check current pricing on the vendor site for plan prices.

**Strengths:** Gamma builds the whole deck from one prompt. It also produces web pages and documents from the same editor, so one outline can become a deck and a one-pager.

Editing is card-based and fast. You can ask the AI to rewrite, shorten or restyle a single card without touching the rest.

**Weakness:** Gamma builds decks from web cards that resize freely. PPTX exports can drift from the on-screen layout, so budget time for cleanup if your final file must live in PowerPoint.

Related: [Gamma tool profile](/tools/gamma) and [Gamma alternatives](/alternatives/gamma).

## 2. Plus AI: which AI presentation maker works inside PowerPoint and Google Slides?

Plus AI is the best AI PowerPoint generator for people who want to stay in PowerPoint or Google Slides. It runs as an add-in, so decks are real, editable slides in your own files and templates from the start. Basic costs $10 per user per month billed annually, or $15 monthly, with 1,500 AI credits.

**Best for:** consultants, analysts and corporate teams with mandatory templates.

**Pricing:** Basic $10/user/mo annual, $15 monthly, 1,500 AI credits per month (tasks use roughly 40 to 170 credits). No free plan, only a free trial. Higher tiers: check current pricing on the vendor site.

**Strengths:** There is no export step, because the output already is a PowerPoint or Slides file. That removes the fidelity problem that hurts web-first tools.

It can also rewrite or restructure existing slides, which matters more at work than generating from scratch.

**Weakness:** No free plan, and the design ceiling is your template. If your company template is plain, Plus AI output will be plain too.

Plus AI does not have a TruTool profile yet. Compare it with [Copilot in PowerPoint](https://trutool.co/guides/best-ai-presentation-maker#5-microsoft-copilot-in-powerpoint-which-option-fits-microsoft-365-teams) and [SlidesAI](https://trutool.co/guides/best-ai-presentation-maker#10-slidesai-which-ai-presentation-maker-is-cheapest-for-google-slides) below.

## 3. Canva: which AI presentation maker is best for design and brand kits?

Canva is the best AI presentation maker for design-led decks and brand control. Its AI features sit inside a full design suite, with a huge template library, brand kits on paid plans and easy PPTX download. Canva is free for individuals. Paid prices were not confirmed, so check current pricing on the vendor site.

**Best for:** marketers, creators, teachers and small brands who care how slides look.

**Pricing:** Free for every individual. Pro (individual) and Business (teams) unlock more AI usage, with Canva stating Business gets 20x higher AI usage than Free. Check current pricing on the vendor site.

**Strengths:** Brand kits keep fonts, colours and logos consistent across a team. You also get images, video and social assets in the same place as your deck.

**Weakness:** Canva's AI generation is shallower than dedicated deck builders. You get a nice starting layout, but more manual structuring than with Gamma.

Related: [Canva tool profile](/tools/canva), [Canva alternatives](/alternatives/canva) and [Figma vs Canva](/compare/figma-vs-canva).

## 4. Beautiful.ai: which AI presentation maker suits brand-consistent business decks?

Beautiful.ai suits business teams that need every deck on brand. Its Smart Slides auto-adjust spacing and alignment as you add content, so nobody breaks the layout. Pro costs $14.50 per month billed annually, and Team costs $40 per user per month annually. AI generation is unlimited, with no credit system.

**Best for:** sales, HR and corporate comms teams sending lots of similar decks.

**Pricing:** Pro $14.50/mo billed annually. Team $40/user/mo annually or $50 monthly, for 2 to 20 seats. No free plan; the 14-day trial needs a card and auto-charges.

**Strengths:** Unlimited AI generation removes credit anxiety. Brand controls lock themes so decks look the same whoever builds them.

**Weakness:** Smart Slides restrict freeform layout. If you want to place things exactly where you like, the guardrails feel tight.

Related: [Beautiful.ai tool profile](/tools/beautiful-ai) and [Beautiful.ai alternatives](/alternatives/beautiful-ai).

## 5. Microsoft Copilot in PowerPoint: which option fits Microsoft 365 teams?

Copilot in PowerPoint fits teams already on Microsoft 365 business plans. It drafts decks from a prompt or a Word document and works inside your company templates. The Copilot Business add-on costs $18 per user per month paid yearly, a promo price through 31 Dec 2026 (normally $21), first year only.

**Best for:** companies standardised on Microsoft 365 that want AI without another vendor.

**Pricing:** Copilot Business add-on $18/user/mo paid yearly (promo 1 Jul to 31 Dec 2026, normally $21). Bundles: Microsoft 365 Business Standard with Copilot $23.50, Business Premium with Copilot $32. Requires an eligible Microsoft 365 business plan; business plans cap at 300 users.

**Strengths:** Because it is built into PowerPoint, it keeps data inside your Microsoft tenant, which IT teams like. Turning an existing Word doc into slides is its most useful trick.

**Weakness:** You need a paid Copilot licence on top of Microsoft 365, and the default output looks plain next to Gamma or Beautiful.ai.

When is a standalone tool still worth it? If you need striking design or you present outside your company template, a dedicated AI PowerPoint generator like Plus AI or Gamma will do more.

Related: [Microsoft Copilot](/tools/microsoft-copilot) and [Microsoft PowerPoint](/tools/microsoft-powerpoint).

## 6. Gemini in Google Slides: which option fits Google Workspace teams?

Gemini in Google Slides fits teams already paying for Google Workspace. It adds AI images and writing help inside Slides, so you stay in a tool everyone knows. Gemini in Slides is included only on higher Workspace tiers; Starter does not get it. Dollar prices were not confirmed, so check current pricing on the vendor site.

**Best for:** Google Workspace companies, schools and teams that share decks in Drive.

**Pricing:** No free tier, 14-day trial. Gemini in Slides appears only on higher Workspace tiers; Starter gets Gemini in Gmail and chat only. Check current pricing on the vendor site.

**Strengths:** No new tool to approve or learn, and decks stay in Drive with normal sharing.

**Weakness:** It works one slide at a time, so building a full, designed deck from one prompt is easier in Gamma.

Related: [Gemini](/tools/gemini), [Google Slides](/tools/google-slides) and [Gemini vs ChatGPT](/guides/gemini-vs-chatgpt).

## 7. Pitch: which AI presentation maker is best for team collaboration?

Pitch is the best AI presentation maker for teams that build decks together. It has live collaboration, comments, reusable templates and analytics on who viewed your deck. The free plan covers up to five members. Plus costs €15 per month and Team €20 per month, both paid yearly, with 500 AI credits monthly.

**Best for:** startups and sales teams who share and track decks.

**Pricing:** Free for up to 5 members and 2 guests. Plus €15/mo and Team €20/mo paying yearly, each with 500 AI credits per month; Business includes 750. Extra credits cost $0.004 each. Prices are shown in EUR; check the vendor site for your currency.

**Strengths:** Live editing, comments and shared templates are built for teams. Presentation analytics tell sales teams which slides prospects actually read.

**Weakness:** AI generation settings are basic. Pitch gives you a decent starting draft, but less control than Gamma over tone and structure.

Related: [Pitch tool profile](/tools/pitch) and [Pitch alternatives](/alternatives/pitch).

## 8. Presentations.ai: which AI presentation maker has the best free plan?

Presentations.ai has the best free plan for occasional users. Starter costs $0 and includes 200 credits with decks up to 20 slides, which is enough for a few real presentations. Pro costs $20 per month billed annually ($240 per year) with 5,000 credits, and prices adjust by country.

**Best for:** students, freelancers and anyone making a deck now and then.

**Pricing:** Starter $0 with 200 credits and up to 20 slides. Pro $20/mo billed annually ($240/yr), 5,000 credits. Gold $100/mo ($1,200/yr), 50,000 credits. Prices shown are US; purchasing-power pricing means readers in India and other regions may see lower prices.

**Strengths:** A real free tier, plus regional pricing that makes paid plans more affordable outside the US.

**Weakness:** The Starter cap of 20 slides and 200 credits runs out fast, and decks can share a similar look.

Related: [Presentations.ai tool profile](/tools/presentations-ai) and [Presentations.ai alternatives](/alternatives/presentations-ai).

## 9. Prezi: which AI presentation maker suits non-linear talks?

Prezi suits speakers who want non-linear, zooming presentations. Its AI turns an outline into a canvas you move around, which works well for talks, lectures and storytelling. A free Basic option exists. Paid tier prices were not confirmed, so check current pricing on the vendor site.

**Best for:** teachers, keynote speakers and video presenters.

**Pricing:** Free Basic plan available. Check current pricing on the vendor site for paid tiers.

**Strengths:** Zoom-based storytelling makes talks memorable, and Prezi Video lets you present over your camera feed.

**Weakness:** The format does not translate to PowerPoint well, and free plan output is limited compared with paid tiers. Confirm free plan limits on the vendor site.

Related: [Prezi tool profile](/tools/prezi) and [Prezi alternatives](/alternatives/prezi).

## 10. SlidesAI: which AI presentation maker is cheapest for Google Slides?

SlidesAI is the cheapest way to add AI deck generation to Google Slides. It runs as an add-on, turning pasted text into slides inside your own file. Basic is free with 200 AI credits per month, and Pro costs $10 per user per month billed at $120 per year, excluding tax.

**Best for:** students, teachers and solo users on Google Slides.

**Pricing:** Basic $0 with 200 AI credits per month and 2,500-character input. Pro $10/user/mo billed $120/yr (30,000 credits per year). Premium $20.83/mo billed $250/yr (84,000 credits per year). Monthly prices: check current pricing on the vendor site.

**Strengths:** Low price, no new editor, and the output is native Google Slides you can share in Drive.

**Weakness:** Designs are simple and there is no dedicated team plan, so it suits individuals more than companies.

SlidesAI does not have a TruTool profile yet. Compare it with [Gemini in Google Slides](https://trutool.co/guides/best-ai-presentation-maker#6-gemini-in-google-slides-which-option-fits-google-workspace-teams) and [Plus AI](https://trutool.co/guides/best-ai-presentation-maker#2-plus-ai-which-ai-presentation-maker-works-inside-powerpoint-and-google-slides).

## What are the best free AI presentation makers?

The best free AI presentation maker options are Presentations.ai, Gamma, Canva and SlidesAI. Presentations.ai gives 200 credits and 20 slides, Gamma gives 400 one-time credits, Canva is free for individuals, and the SlidesAI add-on refreshes 200 credits monthly. Pitch is free for small teams up to five members.

Watch the difference between one-time and monthly credits. Gamma's free credits never refresh, while SlidesAI's reset each month, so for steady light use SlidesAI goes further.

Beautiful.ai and Plus AI have no free plan. Their trials need a card and can auto-charge, so set a reminder.

Bench picks worth knowing: NotebookLM can draft slides grounded in your own documents, and [Slidebean](/tools/slidebean) targets startup pitch decks. Chronicle is also popular for widget-style decks.

## What does an AI presentation maker really cost for a team?

A team of five pays very different amounts depending on seat rules. Using verified annual prices, Plus AI Basic costs $600 a year, SlidesAI Pro $600, the Copilot add-on $1,080 at the promo rate and Beautiful.ai Team $2,400. Pitch, Gamma and Canva team totals depend on seat rules, so check vendors.

| Tool | Plan | Verified price | Five users, one year | Caveat |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Plus AI | Basic | $10/user/mo annual | $600 | Higher tiers unverified |
| SlidesAI | Pro | $10/user/mo annual | $600 | No team plan, per-user licences |
| Microsoft Copilot | Business add-on | $18/user/mo annual | $1,080 | Promo to 31 Dec 2026, first year only; needs an M365 business plan on top |
| Pitch | Team | €20/mo yearly | Check on vendor | Confirm whether price is per member or per workspace |
| Beautiful.ai | Team | $40/user/mo annual | $2,400 | 2 to 20 seats; one card says "includes 3 users" |
| Gamma | Business | Check on vendor | Check on vendor | Shared credit pool; third-party reports of a seat minimum, unverified |
| Canva | Business | Check on vendor | Check on vendor | Prices unverified |

Copilot is not the cheap option it looks like. The $18 is an add-on, so you also pay for an eligible Microsoft 365 business plan.

Seat minimums are the biggest trap. Third-party sources report Gamma Business requires a minimum seat count, which would mean a five-person team pays for unused seats. We could not confirm this on Gamma's site, so ask sales before you buy.

Credits also differ. Gamma's Business plan pools credits across the team, while Plus AI, Pitch and SlidesAI give credits per user.

## How do you choose the right AI presentation maker?

Choose the right AI presentation maker by starting with where your final deck must live. If it must be a PowerPoint or Google Slides file, use Plus AI, Copilot, Gemini or SlidesAI. If design and speed matter more, use Gamma or Canva. Then check free limits, seat rules and export quality before paying.

Ask these questions in order:

1. **Where does the deck end up?** Client wants PPTX: favour add-ins. Shared link is fine: Gamma or Pitch.
2. **What do you already pay for?** Microsoft 365 or Workspace users should try Copilot or Gemini first.
3. **Do you need brand control?** Beautiful.ai and Canva lead here.
4. **How often do you present?** Occasional users can stay on Presentations.ai, Gamma or SlidesAI free plans.
5. **How big is the team?** Check seat minimums and whether credits are pooled.

Run the same short prompt through two or three finalists on free plans or trials, then open the export in PowerPoint. That single check catches most regrets.

For more, see the [presentations category](/categories/presentations), [choosing presentation software](/community/choosing-presentations) and the [presentation tools workflow](/community/presentation-tools-workflow) discussion.

## FAQ

### What is the best free AI presentation maker?

Presentations.ai is the best free AI presentation maker for most people, with 200 credits and decks up to 20 slides at $0. Gamma is a strong alternative with 400 one-time credits, Canva is free for individuals, and SlidesAI refreshes 200 credits every month inside Google Slides. Check limits before relying on any free plan.

### Which AI PowerPoint generator makes editable slides?

The best AI PowerPoint generator for editable slides is Plus AI, because it works inside PowerPoint and Google Slides and outputs native slides in your own template. Microsoft Copilot in PowerPoint does the same for Microsoft 365 users. Web-first tools like Gamma export PPTX files, but layouts can shift and need cleanup.

### Can ChatGPT make a PowerPoint presentation?

ChatGPT can write a slide outline, speaker notes and slide text, and in some setups generate a basic PPTX file. It is not a dedicated presentation designer, so layouts are simple. Many people draft the content in ChatGPT, then paste it into Gamma, Plus AI or Canva to build the finished, designed deck.

### Is Gamma better than Canva for presentations?

Gamma is better than Canva for generating a full deck quickly from one prompt, because its AI builds structure, text and layout together. Canva is better for design control, brand kits and pairing slides with social or video assets. Choose Gamma for speed and Canva when visual polish and brand consistency matter most.

### Does PowerPoint have built-in AI?

Yes. Microsoft Copilot works inside PowerPoint and can draft a deck from a prompt or a Word document. It needs a paid Copilot licence on top of an eligible Microsoft 365 business plan. The Copilot Business add-on costs $18 per user per month paid yearly, a promo running through 31 Dec 2026.

### Are AI-generated presentations good enough for work?

AI-generated presentations are good enough for work as a first draft that you then edit. They save hours on structure and layout, but you still need to check facts, tighten wording and match your brand. Tools that output native PowerPoint or Google Slides files make that final editing pass much faster.
